nodes.label: Booking & Appointment Management System (MVP)
nodes.author: AmmarDw
nodes.rationale: Chosen from model #1 of the AI MVP Bootcamp brochure; scope = user registration, service/appointment display, booking management from a dashboard, and confirmation notification.

nodes.label: conversation_history.md Document Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth surviving context-window limits, session resets and model switches; chat stays a minimal pointer, all prompts/responses live in the file.

nodes.label: PROJECT_REPORT.md (single graded deliverable)
nodes.rationale: One report with TOC: instructions -> template -> generic example -> actual booking-system data, so trainees see both the pattern and a filled example.

nodes.label: research_plan.md (research spikes R1-R4)
nodes.rationale: Registered spikes: R1 Google Meet feasibility, R2 admin dashboard patterns, R3 landing-page sections, R4 calendar UX.

nodes.label: .claude/rules/bootcamp-mvp-process.md
nodes.rationale: Deliberately kept generic so any bootcamp trainee project can use it to guide Claude.

nodes.label: Global i18n + directionality rule
nodes.rationale: Improved, context7-verified rewrite of the legacy i18n_context_system.md blueprint, promoted to a global rule file.

nodes.label: AI_MVP_Bootcamp_6_Days_AR.pdf
nodes.rationale: 6 days / 36h, teams of 2-3, 3-5 core features, demo data only; evaluation weights drive what the docs emphasise.

nodes.label: Lightweight, audience-appropriate documentation stance
nodes.rationale: Target audience is entrepreneurs/students/beginner-intermediate devs, not experts; the capstone report is a style reference only, never a depth target.

nodes.label: User entity (single entity with role field)
nodes.rationale: A separate Provider entity was dropped: one User + a role field (CONSUMER/PROVIDER/ADMIN) covers every case without duplicating identity.
nodes.norm_label: user entity (single entity with role field)

nodes.label: UserService N:M (which services a provider offers)
nodes.rationale: Implemented as a plain @ManyToMany rather than a junction entity, since the join table carries no extra columns.
nodes.norm_label: userservice n:m (which services a provider offers)

nodes.label: Service entity
nodes.rationale: Class name intentionally matches the domain/ERD term even though it collides with Spring's @Service annotation; the project sidesteps this by using @Component for business beans.

nodes.label: GoogleAccountConnection entity
nodes.rationale: Holds userId, googleEmail, encrypted refresh token, scope, connectedAt and a nullable fallbackMeetUrl so a provider is bookable either via OAuth or a pasted persistent link.

nodes.label: AppSettings (single-row typed settings table)
nodes.rationale: application.yaml is read once at startup, packaged in the JAR and often on a read-only filesystem, so it cannot hold a live admin-editable value; a single-row typed table seeded from the yaml default and cached in memory gives one row, one cached read, restart-survival and immediate effect. Live value is cached in memory and refreshed on admin update (AppSettingsCache), so the hot path is one cached read.

nodes.label: Rejected: generic SystemSetting key/value table
nodes.rationale: Over-engineered for a single value; replaced by the typed single-row AppSettings after the user pushed back on adding a whole key/value table for one setting.

nodes.label: Core rule: availability binds to the provider, not the service
nodes.rationale: A provider with 5 daily slots offering 5 services must not appear to have 25 appointments; booking one slot under any service marks it reserved across all that provider's services.
nodes.norm_label: core rule: availability binds to the provider, not the service

nodes.label: uq_provider_slot uniqueness constraint
nodes.rationale: DB-level enforcement of the one-slot-per-provider-per-time rule (FR-4) so overlapping duplicates cannot be created by any code path.

nodes.label: BookingStatus lifecycle (CONFIRMED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED/NO_SHOW/VACANT)
nodes.rationale: Cancel frees the slot back to AVAILABLE, no-show does not (moot anyway, since no-show only applies to past slots that cannot be rebooked); complete/no-show gate on the slot's END time, not its start.

nodes.label: VACANT as a synthesized, never-persisted status
nodes.rationale: A dashboard-only label for open AVAILABLE slots; the V7 CHECK constraint deliberately excludes it so it can never be written even though it is a Java enum value. Added by the V7 migration, whose CHECK constraint deliberately omits VACANT.
nodes.norm_label: vacant as a synthesized, never-persisted status

nodes.label: PATCH /api/bookings/{id}/status role + time gates
nodes.rationale: Enforces role (consumer cancels own >24h out; provider/admin completes after end), time gates, and only-from-CONFIRMED so terminal states are final (409). The UI shadows disallowed buttons but the server is the real gate.

nodes.label: Public landing page
nodes.rationale: Hero -> How-it-works/journey -> Services preview -> FAQ -> Footer; no social-proof section because an MVP has no proof to show.

nodes.label: /book service browsing page (public)
nodes.rationale: Browsing is open; clicking Book when logged out redirects to /sign-in?redirect=/book/{id} so the user returns to exactly where they were. Filtering is a single client-side service-name search box above the grid; no backend query is needed at this scale.

nodes.label: Decision: dedicated booking page, not a modal (R4)
nodes.rationale: The flow is multi-step, the URL should be shareable, and a real route makes the sign-in redirect-back clean.
nodes.norm_label: decision: dedicated booking page, not a modal (r4)

nodes.label: /dashboard shared provider + admin dashboard
nodes.rationale: Same UI for both roles; admin gets extra provider filter/selector. Providers see only their own data, admins see everything. Includes a bookings-over-time chart and a 42-cell (6x7) calendar-aligned month grid sharing one Month/Week/Day granularity toggle, plus role-aware nav.

nodes.label: /appointments 'My Appointments' (consumer-only)
nodes.rationale: Briefly opened to all roles, then reverted to consumer-only: providers/admins already see their own consumer-side bookings merged into /dashboard, so a second page would duplicate data. Direct navigation by a provider/admin redirects to /dashboard.

nodes.label: /dashboard/connect-google provider onboarding screen
nodes.rationale: Three states: not-connected (Connect button + fallback-link paste + not-bookable warning), connected (account email/badge/Disconnect), and a compact dashboard warning banner variant.

nodes.label: Rule: one Claude Design prompt = one screen
nodes.rationale: The combined 'Connect Google + Services mgmt' prompt confused Claude Design about whether to produce one or two artefacts; splitting into single-screen prompts fixed it.
nodes.norm_label: rule: one claude design prompt = one screen

nodes.label: Stacked provider dropdowns for slot selection
nodes.rationale: Chosen over unified admin-defined slots and over a flat time-ordered stack: each provider is a dropdown, several can be open at once to compare, and the list scrolls gracefully as providers grow.
nodes.norm_label: stacked provider dropdowns for slot selection

nodes.label: Calendar pressure colouring (high/medium/low/none)
nodes.rationale: Thresholds: >=4 available = low pressure (green), 3 = medium (amber), 1-2 = about to run out; colours derive from the site palette so they do not disrupt it, reinforced by the number badge and opacity for colourblind safety.

nodes.label: CalendarDayCell design-system component
nodes.rationale: Extended with an optional backward-compatible `total` prop, and later a `full` state so fully-booked days keep their 0/N badge and stay clickable instead of looking empty. Renders the available/total count badge (e.g. 3/8) that FR-9 requires.

nodes.label: Booking success toast (exact text pattern)
nodes.rationale: Auto-dismisses after ~30s with an x to close early. After the redirect change it is carried across via query params which are cleared immediately (router.replace) so a refresh does not re-show it.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay (blurred full-page wait)
nodes.rationale: The Book button triggers a synchronous Google Calendar + email round-trip that is slow enough to feel broken; the page blurs but never disappears so the user keeps context.

nodes.label: '(You)' marker on merged consumer-side rows
nodes.rationale: Only meaningful where the consumer field varies row-to-row, which /appointments can never be; so provider/admin self-bookings merge into /dashboard and render bold + primary-teal with a trailing (You) so they do not read as a real patient.

nodes.label: Provider cannot book their own availability
nodes.rationale: Enforced twice: the signed-in provider's own entry is filtered out of the day-view list client-side, and BookingService rejects it with 400 before any DB write because the client-side filter is not trusted.
nodes.norm_label: provider cannot book their own availability

nodes.label: Shared AppointmentDetailsModal
nodes.rationale: One details view wired into both the consumer /appointments table and the provider/admin dashboard table, rather than two near-duplicate modals; it is the only place the meeting link is surfaced.

nodes.label: Admin-configurable max booking horizon (default 6 months)
nodes.rationale: Bounds how far ahead consumers can book and keeps the year picker down to 1-2 years and the month grid meaningfully shadowed; enforced in both the calendar UI and server-side booking validation.

nodes.label: Provider advance limit = ceil(horizon x 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over doubling: +50% (6 -> 9 months) lets providers pre-load availability ahead of the consumer window without a second admin-facing setting; yaml-only multiplier derived from the admin horizon, and the rolling window makes pre-loaded slots bookable as time advances.

nodes.label: Decision: weekends are not special
nodes.rationale: Hard Fri/Sat skipping was removed because providers already pick weekdays explicitly and some may deliberately work weekends as a part-time job; calendar shadowing is now driven purely by having 0 available slots.

nodes.label: Bulk availability generator (weekdays x date range x time ranges)
nodes.rationale: Available to providers (own slots) and admins (any provider); idempotent re-runs skip existing slots and are bounded by the advance limit.
nodes.norm_label: bulk availability generator (weekdays x date range x time ranges)

nodes.label: Decision: bulk generation is non-destructive
nodes.rationale: A deliberate deviation from the Claude Design copy that said 'conflicts will be replaced' — overwriting would risk deleting already-booked slots.

nodes.label: Decision: provider onboarding is admin-managed (FR-16)
nodes.rationale: Public sign-up always yields CONSUMER; only an admin creates providers or promotes a consumer. Consistent with the admin-controlled services model and gives better vetting; a crafted sign-up requesting PROVIDER is a privilege-escalation attempt and still yields CONSUMER.

nodes.label: Decision: no provider filter on the services grid
nodes.rationale: The journey is service-first: providers only become a filtering concept after a service and date are chosen, and provider-first browsing is unscoped new work, not in FR-1.
nodes.norm_label: decision: no provider filter on the services grid

nodes.label: Monorepo layout (app/backend + app/frontend)
nodes.rationale: One Git repository holding both halves rather than two repos; the nested .git created by create-next-app was removed to keep it single-repo.

nodes.label: GitHub repo AmmarDw/booking-system
nodes.author: AmmarDw
nodes.rationale: Created private, with no README/.gitignore/license init so it would not conflict with the Spring-Initializr-generated files already present locally.

nodes.label: R1 — Google Meet link generation feasibility
nodes.rationale: Feasible on a free Gmail via Google Calendar API + OAuth2 (conferenceData.createRequest, hangoutsMeet); the 'Workspace only' claim applies to the Admin-SDK path, not user OAuth. Custom UI is preserved because the link comes back as a plain string.
nodes.norm_label: r1 — google meet link generation feasibility

nodes.label: R4 — Calendar UX (popup vs dedicated page)
nodes.norm_label: r4 — calendar ux (popup vs dedicated page)

nodes.label: Decision: per-provider Google connection from the start
nodes.rationale: Google marks anyone on the event guest list as Trusted so a single host account would not strictly force manual admits — but that model puts every meeting on an absent operator's calendar and any edge case (different email, waiting room on) could only be cleared by them. Per-provider gives correct ownership and better UX. The userinfo.email scope was added beyond the original spec so the connect screen can show which Google account is connected.
nodes.norm_label: decision: per-provider google connection from the start

nodes.label: Fallback: provider pastes a persistent personal Meet link
nodes.rationale: A provider is not bookable until they either connect Google or set a fallback link; the fallback keeps the booking flow usable without OAuth.
nodes.norm_label: fallback: provider pastes a persistent personal meet link

nodes.label: Spring Boot 4.1.0 backend
nodes.rationale: Docs originally said 'Spring Boot 3'; the Initializr default turned out to be 4.1.0 with 4.x starter names, and the docs were reconciled to reality rather than the plan.

nodes.label: Stateless JWT Bearer authentication
nodes.rationale: Chosen with the user over session auth; security/ package holds JwtService, JwtAuthenticationFilter, AppUserDetailsService, UserPrincipal and CurrentUser. Sits on a stateless Spring Security chain with BCrypt and method security enabled.

nodes.label: SecurityConfig filter chain
nodes.rationale: Needs explicit .exceptionHandling(...) entry points — without them an unauthenticated request has no AuthenticationEntryPoint and surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of 401/403.

nodes.label: Bug: /api/auth/** permitAll leaked /me
nodes.rationale: The wildcard matcher also permitted /api/auth/me, so an anonymous request reached the controller and threw IllegalStateException from CurrentUser.get() instead of a clean 401. Fixed by naming /register and /login explicitly.

nodes.label: GlobalExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice)
nodes.rationale: A bare @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) with no logging silently converted real bugs into opaque 500s; logging was added so that class of bug cannot hide again.

nodes.label: Gotcha: @PreAuthorize denials need their own handler
nodes.rationale: Method-security throws AccessDeniedException inside the MVC handler invocation, so it never reaches SecurityConfig's filter-level accessDeniedHandler; without a dedicated @ExceptionHandler it falls into the catch-all as a 500 instead of 403.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: @preauthorize denials need their own handler

nodes.label: Gotcha: void @DeleteMapping returns 200 + empty body
nodes.rationale: The frontend api() helper only special-cased 204 before calling res.json(), so a successful delete surfaced as a UI error. Fixed on both ends: deletes return ResponseEntity.noContent(), and api() checks response text before parsing regardless of status.

nodes.label: Gotcha: stale inverse-side @ManyToMany in the first-level cache
nodes.rationale: After updating the owning side (User.services) and re-fetching Service in the same persistence context, Hibernate returned the already-loaded instance with a stale providers collection. Fixed by building the response from the known-new set instead of re-querying.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: stale inverse-side @manytomany in the first-level cache

nodes.label: Gotcha: Jackson 3 relocation (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper compiles but throws NoClassDefFoundError at runtime on this stack. Framework-managed JSON is unaffected; fixed by hand-writing the small fixed-shape JSON in the security layer rather than depending on Jackson there at all.

nodes.label: Convention: @Component, never @Service
nodes.rationale: Any class importing the Service entity cannot also import org.springframework.stereotype.Service under its simple name; using @Component everywhere sidesteps the clash uniformly instead of fully-qualifying case by case.

nodes.label: Flyway schema migrations
nodes.rationale: Flyway owns the schema; ddl-auto switched from update to validate so Hibernate only checks that entities match the migrated schema.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Spring Boot 4 moved FlywayAutoConfiguration into its own module
nodes.rationale: A bare flyway-core + flyway-database-postgresql never triggers autoconfiguration — it fails silently, so Flyway had never actually run and the earlier 'migrations applied' claim was unverifiable (no entities existed yet, so validate had nothing to check). Fixed with spring-boot-starter-flyway, keeping flyway-database-postgresql explicit since it is optional inside the starter.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: spring boot 4 moved flywayautoconfiguration into its own module

nodes.label: Demo seed migrations (V2-V6)
nodes.rationale: Demo data only per the bootcamp rule. Bcrypt hashes were extracted from real registrations through the app's own /api/auth/register so they are guaranteed encoder-compatible, rather than hand-computed; a demo admin was seeded as a bootstrapping requirement since only an admin can create users.

nodes.label: Native Windows PostgreSQL 16 service (dev)
nodes.rationale: Docker was planned, but port 5432 was already occupied by an existing native service, so the native install was used instead. DB booking_system is owned by bookingadmin — ownership alone grants public-schema rights on PG15+, so no extra GRANTs are needed.

nodes.label: spring-dotenv (springboot4-dotenv) for local secrets
nodes.rationale: Auto-loads .env as a Spring property source in dev while real environment variables still take precedence, so it stays safe in production and needs no manual shell exports locally.

nodes.label: Rule: real values in .env, placeholders only in .env.example
nodes.rationale: The real DB password had been put in .env.example, which is committed by design; only .env is git-ignored. Caught before the project was even a git repo, so no history needed scrubbing.
nodes.norm_label: rule: real values in .env, placeholders only in .env.example

nodes.label: Gotcha: spring-dotenv loads .env from the process working directory
nodes.rationale: ./mvnw runs from app/backend so it worked, but IntelliJ ran from a different directory, leaving DB_PASSWORD empty -> SCRAM auth failure -> 'Unable to determine Dialect' as a downstream symptom. Fix: set the run config working directory to app/backend.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: spring-dotenv loads .env from the process working directory

nodes.label: BookingService (createBooking)
nodes.rationale: @Transactional; validates slot AVAILABLE, within the booking window, that the provider actually offers the requested service, and that the provider is not booking themselves — then flips the slot to BOOKED. Meeting-link and email failures can never fail the booking itself (NFR-4).

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE slot row lock
nodes.rationale: findByIdForUpdate row-locks the slot so two concurrent bookings cannot both see it as AVAILABLE.
nodes.norm_label: select ... for update slot row lock

nodes.label: Availability month/day endpoints
nodes.rationale: month returns per-day available/total counts; day returns providers grouped with their slots, including only providers with at least one slot that day.

nodes.label: GET /api/settings/booking-window (public)
nodes.rationale: Exposes maxHorizonMonths/today/maxBookableDate (later advanceLimitMonths/maxAdvanceDate) so the frontend can bound calendar navigation without trusting the client clock.

nodes.label: AppointmentQueryService (role-scoped listing)
nodes.rationale: Consumers are hard-scoped server-side to their own consumerUserId so filter params like providerId cannot be used to escape the scope; providers see their provider-scoped rows unioned with bookings they made as a consumer elsewhere. Exposed to the frontend as GET /api/bookings?mine=true, which always returns just the caller's own consumer-side bookings regardless of role.

nodes.label: GET /api/bookings/{feed,stats,chart}
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated multi-value serviceIds/statuses/providerIds plus from/to date range; feed adds synthesized VACANT entries with a negative id and null consumer.

nodes.label: Four date-range-driven stat cards
nodes.rationale: The date range fully replaces the fixed today/this-week/30d windows and the labels adapt. Cards are narrowed by service+provider but deliberately not by the status filter, since each card has an intrinsic status meaning (a no-show rate needs completed+no_show regardless).

nodes.label: Shared dashboard filter system
nodes.rationale: Service / Status / Provider (admin-only) multi-selects plus a date range, applied uniformly to every section so no view can silently show a different slice.

nodes.label: EmailService (Gmail SMTP confirmations)
nodes.rationale: Never throws, per NFR-4. Sends two mails per booking: the consumer confirmation (naming provider name+email) and a separate provider notification (naming consumer name+email) so the provider knows without checking the dashboard. Gmail SMTP on port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS, and the nested spring.mail properties must be written as bracket-quoted YAML keys.

nodes.label: GoogleCalendarService#createMeetingEvent
nodes.rationale: events.insert with conferenceDataVersion=1, hangoutsMeet createRequest, attendees=[consumer, provider] and sendUpdates=all, on the provider's own calendar so they are the organiser who actually attends. Returns null on any failure rather than throwing.

nodes.label: GoogleOAuthService / GoogleOAuthController
nodes.rationale: authorize builds the consent URL with prompt=consent so a refresh token is issued even on reconnect; the callback is public because Google redirects the browser there with no Authorization header.

nodes.label: OAuth state as a short-lived signed JWT
nodes.rationale: Google's callback is a plain browser redirect with no Authorization header, so the JWT filter cannot tell which provider initiated it; a 10-minute purpose-tagged token carrying the provider's user id, signed with the existing key, is the only way to identify them.
nodes.norm_label: oauth state as a short-lived signed jwt

nodes.label: Gotcha: OAuth callback params must be optional
nodes.rationale: A provider clicking Cancel on the consent screen redirects back with error=access_denied and no code param at all; required @RequestParams turned the single most common non-happy path into a raw 500. Caught by deliberately curling that exact shape, not by review.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: oauth callback params must be optional

nodes.label: TokenCipher (AES-256-GCM refresh-token encryption)
nodes.rationale: Key derived via SHA-256 of TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY so any non-empty configured string yields a valid 256-bit key.

nodes.label: Google Cloud project + OAuth client setup (U4)
nodes.rationale: The console is console.cloud.google.com — guessed Google subdomains are a phishing pattern. The 'External' tab no longer exists in the new Google Auth Platform UI (it is the Audience setting from the Get Started wizard), and the redirect URI is a text value pasted into Google's form, not a page to visit.
nodes.norm_label: google cloud project + oauth client setup (u4)

nodes.label: Next.js 16 App Router frontend
nodes.rationale: create-next-app default installed 16 / React 19 / Tailwind v4, reconciling the docs that had said 14 — the same reality-over-plan correction made for Spring Boot. AGENTS.md warns it differs from training data; check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing page code.

nodes.label: BookIt design system (src/components/ds)
nodes.rationale: Tokens (availability-pressure colours, teal, light/dark, Arabic RTL typography swap) plus 11 ES-module components with a barrel export; the 4 Claude Design screens are kept as visual reference only because they rely on sandbox globals rather than ES imports. Primary token is teal #0D9488, with availability greens/ambers tuned distinct and reinforced by the number badge and opacity for colourblind safety.

nodes.label: Claude Design (design generation tool)
nodes.rationale: Design-System-first, then a separate generation per screen selecting that system — never in the system's own chat and never reusing one screen's chat, so iteration history from one screen cannot bleed into another.

nodes.label: DesignSync (Claude Design -> repo bridge)
nodes.rationale: The /design-sync skill is user-triggered only and cannot be model-invoked, so components were pulled via the DesignSync tool's get_file plus local writes.

nodes.label: Gotcha: DS component hooks without "use client"
nodes.rationale: Accordion.jsx calls React.useState internally but shipped without the directive, so rendering it from the Server Component landing page threw 'useState is not a function' at build time. Fixed at the component, not worked around at the page.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: ds component hooks without "use client"

nodes.label: Gotcha: public DB-backed pages need force-dynamic
nodes.rationale: The landing page built as a static route, baking in whatever the backend returned at build time; export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' makes the services preview live.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: public db-backed pages need force-dynamic

nodes.label: Gotcha: toLocaleDateString(undefined) uses the OS locale
nodes.rationale: Rendered Arabic month names on a machine with an Arabic OS locale even though no i18n was wired up; always pass an explicit 'en-US' until real i18n exists.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: tolocaledatestring(undefined) uses the os locale

nodes.label: Gotcha: avoid native number/date/time inputs
nodes.rationale: Chromium renders them with the OS locale, producing Arabic-Indic digits and Arabic day/month labels; replaced with type=text plus format placeholders and regex validation. Kept deliberately even where the Claude Design source used native pickers.

nodes.label: src/lib/api.ts fetch wrapper
nodes.rationale: Injects the Bearer token and checks response text before JSON.parse regardless of status, so a 200-with-empty-body cannot throw.

nodes.label: src/lib/auth.tsx (AuthProvider / useAuth)
nodes.rationale: Token store with localStorage persistence; later threaded the user's id through so the UI can answer 'is this row's consumer me' and 'is this provider me'.

nodes.label: Redirect-back after sign-in (?redirect=)
nodes.rationale: FR-2: an unauthenticated user who tries to book is sent to sign-in and returned to exactly the booking flow they were on.

nodes.label: --brand-primary (#223A71)
nodes.rationale: Core navy of the brand pair. Carries the logo and every heading; aliased as --text-heading so components never touch the raw value. Used for slide titles, display type, and mono command text on snow.

nodes.label: --brand-deep (#142447)
nodes.rationale: The darker half of the navy pair. Exists so there is one, and only one, dark slide surface (--surface-slide-dark); white text on it measures 14:1, which survives a projector.

nodes.label: --brand-sky (#38B6D9)
nodes.rationale: The sky accent. Means STRUCTURE, never state: rules/hairline accents, buttons, technical detail, bullet dots. Also the focus ring. Paired against teal so a single slide never uses two accents for the same meaning.

nodes.label: --brand-teal (#16C7B7)
nodes.rationale: The teal accent. Means STATE, never structure: current step, completed, progress. Kept distinct from sky so progress indication is never confused with decoration.

nodes.label: Raw brand palette (navy pair + sky + teal)
nodes.rationale: The four core swatches: brand-primary #223A71, brand-deep #142447, brand-sky #38B6D9, brand-teal #16C7B7. This is the raw layer -- components are forbidden from referencing it directly and must go through the semantic aliases.
nodes.norm_label: raw brand palette (navy pair + sky + teal)

nodes.label: --brand-white (#FFFFFF)
nodes.rationale: The default light slide surface (--surface-slide) and the invert text colour on dark (--text-invert). Ink on white measures 8.6:1.

nodes.label: --brand-snow (#EEF2F8)
nodes.rationale: The one tint above white. Serves double duty as card surface (--surface-card) and table header (--surface-table-head), and as the background behind mono code blocks -- one tint instead of a grey ramp keeps light surfaces from multiplying.

nodes.label: --brand-snow-line (hairline border)
nodes.rationale: The single 1px separator colour, aliased as --rule-hairline. Because the system caps elevation at a 2px lift, this hairline is what actually delineates cards and swatches -- not shadow.

nodes.label: Card on dark (#1B2E56)
nodes.rationale: The raised card value used on top of the deep slide surface. Sits one step lighter than brand-deep so a card reads as raised without needing a shadow. Not present in the published semantic alias list.

nodes.label: --surface-slide
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-white. The default light slide background.

nodes.label: --surface-slide-dark
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-deep (#142447). The only dark slide surface in the system; carries data-surface="dark" contexts such as the endorsement mark on dark.

nodes.label: --surface-card
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-snow. Card surface on light slides.

nodes.label: --surface-table-head
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-snow. Deliberately the same raw tint as --surface-card: a table header is just another card surface, so no new value is introduced.

nodes.label: --accent-structure
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-sky. Naming the alias 'structure' is what enforces the sky-vs-teal split at the component level.

nodes.label: --accent-state
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-teal. Naming the alias 'state' is what enforces the sky-vs-teal split at the component level.

nodes.label: --text-heading
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-primary. Applied to display and slide-title type; the wordmark overrides it locally to colour the logo.

nodes.label: --text-body
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-ink. Body copy runs at full opacity ink; the system has no dimmed body variant.

nodes.label: --text-invert
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-white. Text colour on the deep surface, where the pairing measures 14:1.

nodes.label: --text-caption
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-ink, i.e. the SAME raw value as --text-body. Captions are separated by size (18px), never by greying the text down -- which is exactly the failure the no-grey-on-white rule forbids.

nodes.label: --rule-hairline
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> snow-line. The only separator token; every card border and table rule goes through it.

nodes.label: --focus-ring
nodes.rationale: Semantic alias -> brand-sky. Focus is treated as structure (an affordance), not as state, which is why it takes sky and not teal.

nodes.label: Rule: components reference semantic aliases, never the raw palette
nodes.rationale: Twelve aliases sit between components and the four raw brand values. The indirection is the point: a component that asks for --surface-card cannot accidentally re-purpose a brand colour, and the palette can be retuned in one place.
nodes.norm_label: rule: components reference semantic aliases, never the raw palette

nodes.label: Rule: sky = structure, teal = state
nodes.rationale: Sky carries structure -- rules, buttons, technical detail, bullet dots. Teal carries state -- current step, completed, progress. Never the same meaning on one slide: with two accents of similar brightness, a viewer at the back of the room can only tell them apart if each keeps one job.

nodes.label: --brand-ink (body text)
nodes.rationale: The body text colour, always at full opacity. Ink on white measures 8.6:1. Backs both --text-body and --text-caption.

nodes.label: Rule: no grey text on white
nodes.rationale: Light grey (#9AA3B4) on white is marked forbidden -- 'projector eats this'. Two sanctioned pairings only: full-opacity ink on white (8.6:1) and white on deep (14:1). De-emphasis must come from size or weight, never from lowering contrast.
nodes.norm_label: rule: no grey text on white

nodes.label: --state-warning (#A96504)
nodes.rationale: The only amber in the system, and an explicit addition to the brand palette -- added solely because callout(warning) needs an amber tone. Deliberately dark enough (#A96504, not a bright yellow) to hold white text and to survive a projector.

nodes.label: --state-warning-soft (#FBF0DC)
nodes.rationale: Tinted fill for the warning callout body, paired with the strong amber on the leading edge. Keeps the callout readable in ink while still reading as a warning.

nodes.label: Warning callout pattern
nodes.rationale: Soft amber fill + a 6px border-inline-start in the strong amber + a bold amber label. The accent bar uses the logical inline-start edge so it flips automatically under RTL/LTR rather than being pinned left.

nodes.label: radius-sm (8px)
nodes.rationale: Smallest corner radius, for tight elements and inline chips.

nodes.label: radius-md (14px)
nodes.rationale: Default card radius -- the value most cards and callouts in the system use.

nodes.label: radius-lg (24px)
nodes.rationale: Large radius for full-bleed panels and hero blocks.

nodes.label: radius-pill (999px)
nodes.rationale: Fully rounded, for badges, tags, and progress bars such as the teal state pills.

nodes.label: Radius scale (sm / md / lg / pill)
nodes.rationale: Four fixed radii -- 8 / 14 / 24 / 999px. A closed set, so nothing in the deck invents an in-between corner.

nodes.label: --lift-1
nodes.rationale: The lighter of the two shadows. Depth is carried mainly by the hairline border; the shadow only hints at separation.

nodes.label: --lift-2
nodes.rationale: The heaviest shadow the system owns -- the ceiling, not a mid step.

nodes.label: Rule: max 2px lift
nodes.rationale: 'Max 2px lift. Nothing heavier exists in this system.' Only two shadow tokens exist, so a designer cannot escalate depth; hierarchy has to come from surface colour, radius, and the hairline rule instead. Heavy shadows also smear on a projector.

nodes.label: Rule: logical properties only
nodes.rationale: Use margin-inline-start, padding-inline-end, text-align:start (and inset-inline) -- never left/right physical properties. The whole deck is authored dir="rtl", so a physical property is a latent bug the moment anything is mirrored.

nodes.label: Rule: what stays LTR inside RTL
nodes.rationale: Two deliberate exceptions to the mirror: file trees are forced dir="ltr", and commands plus reference numbers stay LTR. Mirroring a path or a shell command would make it wrong, not just odd -- so these are pinned rather than flipped.
nodes.norm_label: rule: what stays ltr inside rtl

nodes.label: --brand-teal-soft
nodes.rationale: Soft teal tint used as the fill of a 'rule' callout, with a 6px border-inline-start in full teal -- the same callout shape as the amber warning, tinted for a positive/rule note instead of a caution.

nodes.label: Spacing scale (8px base, 8 steps)
nodes.rationale: sp-1 8, sp-2 16, sp-3 24, sp-4 32, sp-5 48, sp-6 64, sp-7 96, sp-8 128. Rule: 'gaps only, never per-element margins' -- spacing is owned by the container's gap, so no element carries its own margin and nothing collapses or double-spaces when blocks are reordered.

nodes.label: Slide geometry (1920x1080, 96px safe, 96px footer)
nodes.rationale: Fixed 16:9 1920x1080 frame with a 96px (5%) safe margin on all sides and a 96px footer zone at the bottom. Both the margin and the footer are 5% of the frame, expressed as sp-7, so slide geometry lands on the same 8px grid as component spacing. Drawn with inset-inline so it holds under RTL.

nodes.label: display (68px / 700)
nodes.rationale: Cover-slide title only. 68px bold, line-height 1.2, IBM Plex Sans Arabic, coloured brand-primary.

nodes.label: slide-title (42px / 700)
nodes.rationale: The single title on a content slide -- 'the only heading in the slide'. 42px bold, line-height 1.28, brand-primary. One title per slide is a structural rule, not just a size.

nodes.label: section-number (20px / 600)
nodes.rationale: The section badge, e.g. 'القسم 7.10'. Small but semibold so the number reads as a marker rather than as body copy.

nodes.label: body-lead (29px / 500)
nodes.rationale: The one main line of a slide. 29px, weight 500, line-height 1.7 -- one step up from body so the key sentence is found before the bullets.

nodes.label: body (23px / 400)
nodes.rationale: Bullets and cards. 23px regular, line-height 1.75, measure capped around 52ch. The 1.75 leading is required for Arabic diacritics, and the 23px size sits above the 22px projector floor.

nodes.label: caption (18px / 400)
nodes.rationale: Labels and footnotes -- the only role allowed below the 22px body floor. It buys that exemption by staying full-opacity brand-ink: smaller, never greyer.

nodes.label: mono (20px / 400, IBM Plex Mono, forced LTR)
nodes.rationale: Commands and paths. 20px IBM Plex Mono in brand-primary on a snow block, always dir="ltr" -- a shell command reordered by the RTL algorithm would be wrong, not merely ugly.
nodes.norm_label: mono (20px / 400, ibm plex mono, forced ltr)

nodes.label: Type scale (7 roles, projector-sized)
nodes.rationale: Seven roles: display 68/700, slide-title 42/700, section-number 20/600, body-lead 29/500, body 23/400, caption 18/400, mono 20/400. Every size is 'sized for a projector at the back of the room' -- the scale starts far larger than a screen-first scale would, which is also why the body floor is 22px and why grey text is banned.

nodes.label: --font-arabic (IBM Plex Sans Arabic)
nodes.rationale: The single text face for every Arabic role from display down to caption. One family across the whole scale, so hierarchy comes only from size and weight.

nodes.label: --font-mono (IBM Plex Mono)
nodes.rationale: Companion monospace face, matched to IBM Plex Sans Arabic. Used for commands, paths, token names, and hex values -- everything that must be read literally, and therefore everything that is forced dir="ltr".

nodes.label: Rule: Arabic body line-height 1.75
nodes.rationale: Body runs at 1.75; below 1.7 Arabic diacritics collide with the line above. The card contrasts 1.75 (correct) against 1.25 (broken). This is a script-specific constraint, not a taste preference -- a Latin-derived 1.4 would be unreadable here.

nodes.label: Rule: body never below 22px
nodes.rationale: A hard floor for body copy on slides -- 23px body sits just above it. Prevents the usual fix of shrinking type to fit more content; the content has to be cut instead.

nodes.label: Rule: wrap every Latin fragment in an RTL line
nodes.rationale: Latin words and commands inside Arabic text must be wrapped in .tok-lat / .tok-code so they cannot reorder the line. Unwrapped, the bidi algorithm moves punctuation and slashes to the wrong end and 'the line breaks apart' -- shown side by side on the card.
nodes.norm_label: rule: wrap every latin fragment in an rtl line

nodes.label: .tok-lat (Latin fragment wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Wrapper for Latin words inside Arabic prose, e.g. 'Claude Code'. Isolates the run so it keeps its own direction.

nodes.label: .tok-code (inline command wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Wrapper for inline commands and slash-commands inside Arabic prose, e.g. '/init'. Without it the leading slash jumps to the wrong end of the phrase.

nodes.label: Wordmark zone (placeholder)
nodes.rationale: .sag-logo / .sag-logo__wordmark in two sizes (standard, footnote), coloured via a local --text-heading override. Explicitly a TYPE-SET STAND-IN: the real letterforms are hand-drawn calligraphy that was never supplied, and the card carries a warning callout saying to swap in the original file when it arrives.

nodes.label: Endorsement mark (placeholder)
nodes.rationale: .sag-endorse -- an 'S' mark plus a bilingual lockup (SAG TECH / ساج التقنية) shown at footer size on both the light card and the deep dark surface. Proves the mark holds at its smallest size on both surfaces; also a placeholder.

nodes.label: Title slide reference screen
nodes.rationale: Standalone 1920x1080 ar/rtl harness that renders only the title frame from the shared deck fixture, so the cover can be reviewed in isolation from the nine-frame walkthrough.

nodes.label: SlideTitle frame (cover)
nodes.rationale: Cover anatomy is fixed: hero wordmark, program line, subtitle, presenter block (name/role/org) and the endorsement org line - so every day of the bootcamp opens identically.

nodes.label: SlideSection frame (divider)
nodes.rationale: Puts the big curriculum number above the Arabic title on a dark surface: the number is the trainee position marker in the curriculum, and the dark surface signals a hard break between sections rather than another content slide.

nodes.label: SlideContent frame (workhorse)
nodes.rationale: The workhorse frame: one badge, one heading, a lead line and bullets, with a focusIndex that highlights exactly one bullet - one idea per slide, one emphasis per idea. Accepts a nested Callout for the rule that must not be missed.

nodes.label: SlideSplit frame (comparison)
nodes.rationale: Two mirrored columns keyed start/end rather than left/right, so the comparison keeps its reading order under RTL; used for you-versus-Claude style contrasts.

nodes.label: SlideMedia frame (media-dominant)
nodes.rationale: Declared the most used frame in the hands-on section: the screenshot carries the teaching, so the media area dominates and text shrinks to one instruction plus a caption. Numbered callouts are pinned by percentage x/y so they survive rescaling of the 1920x1080 stage.

nodes.label: SlideSteps frame (numbered sequence)
nodes.rationale: Vertical numbered sequence with per-step states and an activeIndex, so the trainee sees the whole flow before the work and knows which step is current - each step carries a short note instead of a paragraph.

nodes.label: SlideTable frame (reference table)
nodes.rationale: Compact reference table with a snow header, declared column widths, a numeric column flag and a focusRow - built for a slide trainees are told to keep and come back to, not for dense data.

nodes.label: SlideQuote frame (single statement)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately the only centred frame in the whole system - centring is reserved as the signal that this slide carries one rule and nothing else.

nodes.label: SlideClosing frame (end of day)
nodes.rationale: Splits the day close into what was accomplished (icon skill cards in a done state) and what comes next (plain bullets), so the trainee leaves with proof of progress plus tomorrow's frame; carries a 100% DayProgress.

nodes.label: Deck walkthrough screen (index)
nodes.rationale: One screen that clicks through all nine frames in order with arrow keys or the pill nav, so the frame vocabulary is reviewed as a deck rather than as nine isolated cards; the footer keeps day + slide number visible throughout.

nodes.label: Scale-to-fit 1920x1080 stage harness
nodes.rationale: Slides are authored at a fixed 1920x1080 canvas but reviewed in an arbitrary browser window, so fit() computes min(w/1920,(h-90)/1080), sizes the clipping box and CSS-scales the stage; transform-origin is top right because the deck is RTL, and it is re-run on load, resize and via ResizeObserver.

nodes.label: Shared deck fixture (SAG_SLIDES)
nodes.rationale: All ten screens load the same Babel-compiled fixture and pick their slide by id, so sample content (Day 7, presenter, section 7.10) is authored once; the SAG_ON_SLIDES handshake covers the race between the fixture and the host page.

nodes.label: SAGLabDesignSystem_5a6e2d global namespace
nodes.rationale: The compiled design-system bundle exposes every frame and element under one hashed global, which is what lets both the React reference screens and the Claude Design template import the same components without a build step.

nodes.label: RTL logical-direction contract for screens
nodes.rationale: Every screen declares lang=ar dir=rtl on the document itself and positions chrome with logical properties (inset-inline-start, transform-origin top right) rather than left/right, so mirroring is inherited instead of hand-authored per slide.

nodes.label: dsCard screen annotation convention
nodes.rationale: Each reference screen opens with an HTML comment carrying group, viewport and a name/subtitle pair - the subtitle is where the frame's intent is recorded, so the catalogue can be generated and the why travels with the file.

nodes.label: Bootcamp day deck template
nodes.rationale: A four-slide RTL starting deck (cover, content, media, closing) laid out as stacked artboards on one canvas so a trainer can duplicate a real day and edit it visually instead of writing slide code.

nodes.label: Artboard 01 - cover
nodes.rationale: Dark-surface cover with the hero stacked wordmark, program display, day line and a presenter block that ships with a photo placeholder so the slot is visible before a real photo exists.

nodes.label: Artboard 02 - content slide
nodes.rationale: Static markup of the head (badge, title, rule, lead) plus a bullet list and a Callout, with the same section 7.10 sample the React content frame uses.

nodes.label: Artboard 03 - media slide
nodes.rationale: Media frame plus a side instruction column, badged as a task (14.1) rather than a section - the task badge is what marks a hands-on slide.

nodes.label: Artboard 04 - end of day
nodes.rationale: Dark surface, two labelled groups: done skill cards in a single-column grid for accomplishments, plain bullets for tomorrow.

nodes.label: DCLogic component + props panel
nodes.rationale: Exposes showProgress / activeDay / totalDays / withinDay as editor controls grouped under a Footer section and derives a single progressNode from them, so the trainer retargets the deck to another day from the properties panel instead of editing four footers by hand.

nodes.label: Idempotent Lucide icon loader
nodes.rationale: componentDidMount injects the Lucide UMD script guarded by a fixed element id and forces one re-render on load - the canvas editor can mount the component many times, so the guard prevents duplicate script tags while still guaranteeing icons appear.

nodes.label: ds-base.js design-system loader
nodes.rationale: Deliberately reduces binding the template to a consuming project to editing one base path line; its onerror message spells out the two common relative paths and the not-yet-compiled-bundle case.

nodes.label: FooterBar element
nodes.rationale: Persistent slide chrome carrying day, slide number and an optional progress node - present on every artboard so orientation never depends on the slide body.

nodes.rationale: Two Arabic words stacked at 250px with tightened line-height and negative letter-spacing so the mark reads as one block at any size.

nodes.rationale: A fixed 320px column of teal, sky and deep navy - the palette shown as swatches next to the mark so the thumbnail carries the system's colours, not just its name.

nodes.label: Curriculum docx build pipeline
nodes.rationale: Two steps, both required: a JS generator cannot express the OOXML that Word needs for correct RTL, so a Python post-patch is a mandatory second pass rather than an optional polish.

nodes.label: build.js (Markdown to raw .docx)
nodes.rationale: Step one: converts the Arabic curriculum Markdown into raw.docx with the docx npm package, emitting bidi paragraphs without any justification.

nodes.label: rtl_patch.py (OOXML RTL post-patch)
nodes.rationale: Exists purely to add what docx-js cannot express - section-level bidi, docDefaults RTL, a real Normal style and RTL TOC styles - and to strip any leftover physical justification.

nodes.label: raw.docx intermediate
nodes.rationale: Never the deliverable - it is the un-patched hand-off between the two required steps.

nodes.label: The OOXML RTL trap (w:jc is start/end)
nodes.rationale: w:jc in OOXML is logical start/end, not physical left/right: inside a paragraph carrying w:bidi, w:jc=right means end, which renders on the LEFT. So bidirectional:true together with alignment:RIGHT produces left-aligned Arabic - the exact bug the two-script pair exists to fix.
nodes.norm_label: the ooxml rtl trap (w:jc is start/end)

nodes.label: Rule: bidi paragraphs omit w:jc entirely
nodes.rationale: RTL paragraphs set w:bidi and write no justification at all, because the default (start) already resolves to right under bidi - stating alignment can only re-introduce the trap.
nodes.norm_label: rule: bidi paragraphs omit w:jc entirely

nodes.label: Patch: w:bidi in sectPr
nodes.rationale: Sets section/page reading order; without it tab stops and table column order stay LTR even when the paragraphs are right.

nodes.label: Patch: w:bidi + w:rtl in docDefaults
nodes.rationale: Makes anything unstyled inherit RTL instead of falling back to LTR.

nodes.label: Patch: define a real RTL Normal style
nodes.rationale: docx-js emits headings with basedOn=Normal but never defines Normal, so the inheritance chain dangles until the patch supplies it.
nodes.norm_label: patch: define a real rtl normal style

nodes.label: Patch: RTL TOC1-TOC3 styles
nodes.rationale: Word builds TOC entries from these styles at open time, so they have to already be RTL in styles.xml - patching the document body is too late.

nodes.label: Guard: strip w:jc=right from bidi paragraphs
nodes.rationale: Defensive sweep in case any physical justification survived generation - the failure it prevents is silent, so it is cheaper to always strip.
nodes.norm_label: guard: strip w:jc=right from bidi paragraphs

nodes.label: Deliberate LTR exceptions
nodes.rationale: Directory trees (detected by the box-drawing characters) and shell commands stay LTR because mirroring them destroys their meaning; Arabic prose inside fenced blocks is still rendered RTL.

nodes.label: Structural verification check
nodes.rationale: No LibreOffice or pdftoppm on the machine, so there is no visual render step; correctness is proved structurally instead - heading and table counts must match the Markdown and the count of w:jc=right must be exactly 0.

nodes.label: Git identity is metadata; GitHub auth is a stored token
nodes.rationale: user.name/user.email are stamped into each commit and never verified by Git. Authentication is a token: Git Credential Manager opens an OAuth page in the browser on the first push and stores the token in Windows Credential Manager. The trainer never saw the OAuth page because a token was already stored; a fresh trainee machine will certainly stop there.
nodes.norm_label: git identity is metadata; github auth is a stored token

nodes.label: GitHub private noreply email option
nodes.rationale: Commit emails live in history forever; course repos are private, but a later public repo would expose the real email. GitHub Settings > Emails > 'Keep my email addresses private' gives ID+username@users.noreply.github.com, optional and free, with a 'Block command line pushes that expose my email' companion. Verified against GitHub's official docs.

nodes.label: Fix: tok-code overflow-wrap:anywhere
nodes.rationale: Measured scrollWidth 686 vs clientWidth 605 on slide 34: a long noreply address was one unbreakable word that set min-content, and overflow-y:auto clips both axes so a horizontal bar appeared. Fixed globally in tokens/rtl.css with overflow-wrap:anywhere (not break-word, which does not shrink min-content). .snip was not part of the problem.

nodes.label: Mixed-resolution concat: re-encode only old clip
nodes.rationale: git-auth.mp4 was 1080p and git.mp4 720p, so stream-copy concat would break. Re-encode git.mp4 alone (lanczos upscale to 1920x1080, x264 CRF 18) and stream-copy the new clip so the important one keeps original sharpness. Verified by frame count (1521+1684=3205) and four frame fingerprints matched at +1521 frames; offset 50.70 s.
nodes.norm_label: mixed-resolution concat: re-encode only old clip

nodes.label: Gotcha: MSYS paths + exit 0 on failed concat
nodes.rationale: An MSYS-style path (/c/Users/...) inside the concat list was read by the Windows ffmpeg as relative (C:/c/Users/...), and ffmpeg still exited 0 although the join failed. Caught by checking duration (50.74 instead of 106.92), not the exit code. Use absolute Windows paths.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: msys paths + exit 0 on failed concat

nodes.label: Lesson: empty extractions compare as identical

nodes.norm_label: lesson: empty extractions compare as identical

nodes.label: Skill output must be eye-checkable
nodes.rationale: The brochure says no applied programming experience is needed, and five of seven audience segments cannot read code, so any taught skill must produce something judged by looking. This removes code review, testing, refactoring and security-audit ideas, and the block goes beyond the brochure, which only promises using Rules/Skills/MCP.

nodes.label: 238-skill defect study (arXiv 2607.01456)
nodes.rationale: Empirical study of 238 real skills: over 99% carry a defect — 94% nothing stops skipping a step, 78% no planning stage, 77% never ask a human, 69% no validation, 67% no 'must not' list, 34% no example, 32% prose instead of numbered steps, under 1% too long. Beginners fear writing too much; the data says fear leaving things out.

nodes.label: van Gog 2011: worked example first
nodes.rationale: van Gog, Kester & Paas (2011): worked-example-first and example-then-problem orderings significantly outperformed problem-first for novices; never open with 'try it yourself, we'll show you after'.

nodes.label: Analogical encoding: compare two cases
nodes.rationale: Loewenstein, Thompson & Gentner: comparing two partly understood examples surfaces shared structure (about 3x more likely to apply later); Rittle-Johnson & Star: concurrent beats sequential, and fewer types helps low-prior-knowledge learners.

nodes.label: Renkl & Atkinson backward fading
nodes.rationale: Move from full example to completion problem to independence, dropping the last steps first; so the description line, the highest-load lowest-value thing to write cold, ships as a template with marked blanks.

nodes.label: Patall meta-analysis: 2–4 choices
nodes.rationale: Patall, Cooper & Robinson (41 studies): choice raises motivation and performance, strongest at 2-4 meaningful options; Carpentries practice adds three formative checkpoints per hour.

nodes.label: Derive method by comparing two own skills
nodes.rationale: Do not explain the abstraction: put writing-requirements (a writing/elicitation procedure) and drawio (a tool-driving skill) side by side and ask for three shared things. Trainees reliably produce trigger line, numbered steps, a rule about what not to do and a definition of done — the method, written by them, at zero new teaching material.
nodes.norm_label: derive method by comparing two own skills

nodes.label: Two skill types: procedure vs tool-running
nodes.rationale: Teach two types only (procedure-only; tool-running) because fewer types helps low-prior-knowledge learners; the code-bearing variant gets one sentence. A change from the TODO's three or four types.
nodes.norm_label: two skill types: procedure vs tool-running

nodes.label: The six skill slots
nodes.rationale: When it runs, what it does, what it needs (the only slot that changes with type), numbered steps 3-7, where to stop and ask me, and when it counts as done plus one example. Ordered to front-load what real skills omit; reconciles the transcript's framework with skill-creator's Capture Intent. The transcript's sixth item (progressive updates) is only a closing remark.

nodes.label: Decision: one recording, no live re-run
nodes.rationale: One recording shows one skill end to end including running it and fixing it once; no live re-run, because a section whose task is one-time is watched, not re-run (the section 16 precedent in day-deck-recipe.md) and the worked example must precede building. Live minutes go to the comparison exercise and vetting each trainee's idea. Two recordings rejected.
nodes.norm_label: decision: one recording, no live re-run

nodes.label: Six vetted ideas or own idea via seven gates
nodes.rationale: A menu alone kills ownership, free choice produces the traps. The boundary: seven yes/no gates (done by hand 3 times, trigger sentence, 3-7 steps, no new account or key, output judged in under a minute, a one-line success test, one real example). Any 'no' means take a menu item; the trainer approves before building.
nodes.norm_label: six vetted ideas or own idea via seven gates

nodes.label: Pre-commit in 5 minutes + disposability line
nodes.rationale: Everyone writes their choice in the first five minutes with no renegotiation after minute 8 — the highest-leverage anti-overrun measure — and the trainer says 'مهارتك اليوم مسوّدة أولى — الطريقة هي اللي تطلع بها', the cheapest anxiety reducer for non-programmers.

nodes.label: CSS .snip--rtl and .snip--scroll

nodes.rationale: -ss (before or after -i) zeroed the actual PTS for this specific file — confirmed via the showinfo filter returning pts_time:0 for every nonzero requested offset. nodes.label: Claude Design (أداة)
nodes.rationale: أداة في claude.ai تولّد الواجهات وتكرّرها بصريًا؛ ترسم شكل الشاشة وحالاتها، لا السلوك/المنطق الذي يُبنى لاحقًا في الكود.

nodes.label: نظام التصميم (Design System)
nodes.rationale: أساس موحّد: ألوان وخطوط ومسافات وزوايا زائد مكوّنات جاهزة؛ يُبقي كل الشاشات متّسقة؛ هو الوحيد الذي ينتقل تلقائيًّا إلى المشروع عبر DesignSync.

nodes.label: DesignSync (الجسر)
nodes.rationale: الجسر الذي يقرأ به Claude مكوّنات نظام التصميم وألوانه وخطوطه وينقلها للمشروع تلقائيًّا، بلا تدخّل من المتدرّب.

nodes.label: مكوّنات جاهزة (Components)
nodes.rationale: عناصر واجهة متكرّرة تُبنى مرّة واحدة في نظام التصميم وتُستخدم في كل مكان؛ كلما زادت، قلّ ما يُبنى من الصفر لاحقًا.

nodes.label: ما ينتقل تلقائيًّا وما لا ينتقل
nodes.rationale: مكوّنات نظام التصميم تنتقل تلقائيًّا؛ الشاشات المولّدة لا تنتقل وتبقى في Claude Design، يجب تنزيل ملفّاتها يدويًّا. السبب التقني: DesignSync يعمل فقط على مشاريع من نوع Design System، والنوع يُحدَّد عند الإنشاء ولا يتغيّر بعده.
nodes.norm_label: ما ينتقل تلقاييا وما لا ينتقل

nodes.label: RTL (Right-to-Left)
nodes.rationale: الكتابة تبدأ من اليمين وتتّجه لليسار؛ العربية مثال عليه.

nodes.label: LTR (Left-to-Right)
nodes.rationale: الكتابة تبدأ من اليسار وتتّجه لليمين؛ الإنجليزية مثال عليه.

nodes.label: نمط سؤال الفجوة الأخيرة
nodes.rationale: أعلى قيمة من المراجعة ليست مراجعة عمل Claude بل تذكّر ما لا يزال في ذهن المتدرّب فقط؛ الإضافة تُصنَّف بطريقتين: قسم داخل شاشة موجودة (أصله تلك الشاشة)، أو شاشة جديدة كاملة (تحتاج أصلًا كبقية الشاشات — متطلّب يبرّرها).

nodes.label: قاعدة إلزامية — انسخ إجابات النموذج
nodes.rationale: Claude Code يعرف فقط ما طلبه هو في الأمر؛ أي تفصيل يُضاف أثناء توليد الشاشة في Claude Design (إجابة سؤال أو إضافة من المتدرّب) لا يعلمه Claude Code بلا نسخه، فيُهمَل وقت البناء.

nodes.label: كيف توصل شاشتك إلى Claude Code
nodes.norm_label: كيف توصل شاشتك الى claude code

nodes.label: الضغط (Compaction)
nodes.rationale: عند اقتراب نافذة السياق من الامتلاء (~85% افتراضيًا) يلخّص Claude Code أقدم أجزاء المحادثة تلقائيًا؛ قد يختصر تفاصيل قديمة، ولهذا conversation_history.md يبقى المرجع الكامل الذي لا يُختصر.

nodes.label: درس: فروق بين الشاشات المبنية وتصاميم Claude Design
nodes.rationale: بعد بناء الشاشات في الكود وُجدت فوارق ممتدّة عبر خمس صفحات مقارنةً بتصاميم Claude Design الأصلية؛ أُصلحت بإرسال روابط التصميم مرجعًا.
nodes.norm_label: درس: فروق بين الشاشات المبنية وتصاميم claude design

nodes.label: الكيان (Entity)
nodes.rationale: نوع من الأشياء يخزّن المشروع معلومات عنها؛ يتحوّل لاحقًا إلى جدول.

nodes.label: الحقل (Field)
nodes.rationale: معلومة واحدة داخل الكيان؛ يصير عمودًا في الجدول.

nodes.label: العلاقة (Relationship)
nodes.rationale: كيف يرتبط كيان بآخر: 1—N أو N:M.

nodes.label: مفتاح التعريف (Key ID)
nodes.rationale: رقم يميّز كل صفّ في الجدول عن بقية الصفوف؛ Claude يضيفه تلقائيًا لكل كيان؛ يختلف عن مفتاح API (كلمة سرّ لخدمة خارجية).

nodes.label: جدول الربط (Junction Table)
nodes.rationale: جدول يضيفه Claude تلقائيًا لربط كيانين بعلاقة N:M، ويشرح سببه بجملة — لا يُمرَّر صامتًا.

nodes.label: مشروع سابق للمدرب — نظام حجز مواعيد (ثمانية كيانات)
nodes.rationale: نموذج بيانات بثمانية كيانات: المستخدمون (بحقل دور)، الخدمات، ربط المستخدم بالخدمات (جدول ربط N:M)، المواعيد المتاحة، الحجوزات، وغيرها — جدول الربط أضافه Claude تقنيًّا بلا طلب.
nodes.norm_label: مشروع سابق للمدرب — نظام حجز مواعيد (ثمانية كيانات)

nodes.label: ERD (Entity-Relationship Diagram)
nodes.rationale: مخطّط الكيانات والعلاقات: رسمة توضّح كل كيان (صندوق بحقوله داخله) وكيف يرتبط بالكيانات الأخرى.

nodes.label: درس: صناديق كيانات خرجت فارغة رغم سلامة الشكل العام
nodes.rationale: في بناء حقيقي خرجت بعض صناديق الكيانات فارغة تمامًا رغم أن المخطّط بدا سليمًا من بعيد؛ يجب فحص محتوى كل صندوق لا الشكل العام فقط.
nodes.norm_label: درس: صناديق كيانات خرجت فارغة رغم سلامة الشكل العام

nodes.label: context7 (أداة توثيق)
nodes.rationale: يجلب توثيق المكتبات المحدّث تلقائيًا أثناء البناء، بلا أي شيء من المتدرّب.

nodes.label: القسم 14 — دورة العمل الواحدة
nodes.rationale: خمس خطوات لكل وظيفة: تجهيز قطعة التصميم، يبنيها Claude كاملةً، يختبرها Claude (آليًّا وعبر chrome-devtools)، يجرّبها المتدرّب في الواجهة، الحفظ (commit & push) — مرّتان على الأقل: عند إتمام كل وظيفة وفي نهاية كل يوم.

nodes.label: وضع الخطة (plan mode) قبل كل مهمّة
nodes.rationale: اطلب من Claude دخول وضع الخطة فيعرض ملخّصًا بسيطًا بلا مصطلحات قبل التنفيذ.
nodes.norm_label: وضع الخطة (plan mode) قبل كل مهمة

nodes.label: درس: أداة تهيئة الجداول توقّفت دون رسالة خطأ
nodes.rationale: في بناء حقيقي، أداة تهيئة الجداول لم تكن تعمل إطلاقًا دون أي رسالة خطأ؛ بقيت قاعدة البيانات فارغة ولم يُكتشف ذلك إلا بالنظر فيها فعليًّا. «لم يظهر خطأ» لا تعني «نجح».
nodes.norm_label: درس: اداة تهيية الجداول توقفت دون رسالة خطا

nodes.label: قاعدة: مقارنة الجداول الفعلية بالمخطّط — تحديث الفرق فقط
nodes.rationale: بعد إنشاء الجداول، تُقارَن الجداول الفعلية بمخطّط المهمة 13.3 وتُحدَّث الفروق فقط إن وُجدت — لا إعادة رسمه كاملًا من الصفر، لأن ذلك يفقد الترتيب الذي أُنجز في 13.3.
nodes.norm_label: قاعدة: مقارنة الجداول الفعلية بالمخطط — تحديث الفرق فقط

nodes.label: حادثة: اتصال Supabase MCP احتاج تجديدًا أثناء المقطع
nodes.rationale: Claude اكتشف أن اتصال Supabase يحتاج تجديدًا وكتب خطّة جاهزة فورًا بدل التوقّف أو الادّعاء بالنجاح؛ المتدرّب أعاد الاتصال بأمر /mcp ثم «إعادة الاتصال» بلا نسخ أي مفتاح.
nodes.norm_label: حادثة: اتصال supabase mcp احتاج تجديدا اثناء المقطع

nodes.label: مثال: الزرّ المخفي لكنه يحذف العنصر
nodes.rationale: زرّ «حذف العنصر» يظهر للمشرف فقط؛ مستخدم عادي يرسل نفس الطلب مباشرة من أدوات المطوّر، والنظام ينفّذه رغم أنه لم ير الزرّ قط — إخفاء الزرّ لم يُغلق الطريق إلى الوظيفة نفسها.
nodes.norm_label: مثال: الزر المخفي لكنه يحذف العنصر

nodes.label: القيد في الخادم لا الواجهة
nodes.rationale: الكود الذي يتحقّق من دور المستخدم يعمل في الخادم نفسه لا في شاشته؛ القاعدة: لا تثق بالواجهة أبدًا. في الحزمة الافتراضية يحدث في موضعين معًا: كود الموقع وقاعدة البيانات نفسها.

nodes.rationale: من مشروع سابق للمدرب (نظام حجز مواعيد): قاعدة منطقية غائبة ظهرت فقط بالتجريب، ثم مُنعت في الواجهة والخادم معًا.

nodes.label: حادثة: محاولة أولى عادت «مرفوضة» فسأل Claude بدل أن يفترض
nodes.rationale: تبيّن أن «الرفض» كان تحذيرًا تلقائيًّا لا رفضًا حقيقيًّا؛ Claude حقّق في السبب بدل تجاهل رفض غير متوقَّع أو إعادة المحاولة صامتًا.
nodes.norm_label: حادثة: محاولة اولى عادت «مرفوضة» فسال claude بدل ان يفترض

nodes.label: تحذير: /design-sync عكس الاتجاه المطلوب
nodes.rationale: /design-sync يرفع كودًا من المشروع إلى Claude Design — عكس ما يحتاجه المتدرّب هنا تمامًا؛ لا يُشغَّله المتدرّب ولا Claude في هذه الدورة.

nodes.label: قاعدة: رجّعه لمكانه بعد الدخول
nodes.rationale: إن طُلب من زائر تسجيل الدخول في منتصف مسار، يُعاد بعد تسجيله إلى نفس النقطة لا إلى الصفحة الرئيسية من جديد.

nodes.label: المهمة 14.4 — بناء الصفحة الرئيسية والتصفّح العام
nodes.norm_label: المهمة 14.4 — بناء الصفحة الرييسية والتصفح العام

nodes.label: سؤال «لماذا لا؟» — تصفية مقدّم الخدمة
nodes.rationale: المدرب سأل Claude «لماذا لا توجد لدينا تصفية بحسب من يقدّمها؟» فشرح Claude منطقه وبقي القرار على حاله؛ القيمة في فهم السبب لا في تغيير النتيجة بالضرورة.

nodes.label: المحاولة الأولى — بُنيت من غير ملفّات التصميم
nodes.rationale: Claude بنى الشكل من عنده بدل ملفّات التصميم فطلعت صفحة داكنة عامّة؛ المتدرّب رفضها صراحةً؛ صُحِّحت التعليمات بعد المقطع ليصير تنزيل ملفّات كل شاشة الخطوة الأولى لا حلًا احتياطيًا.
nodes.norm_label: المحاولة الاولى — بنيت من غير ملفات التصميم

nodes.label: /design-login حُذف من التعليمات
nodes.rationale: لم يعد خطوة في المهمّة؛ Claude يقرأ نظام التصميم بنفسه، وأقصى ما قد يظهر موافقة في المتصفّح لمرّة واحدة بلا أمر يكتبه المتدرّب.

nodes.label: حادثة: طُلب تشغيل /design-sync بالخطأ لجلب التصميم
nodes.rationale: Claude حاول تشغيله فرفض النظام؛ تبيّن بعد المقطع أن /design-sync معكوس الاتجاه أصلًا (يرفع كودًا إلى Claude Design)؛ حُذف من التعليمات.
nodes.norm_label: حادثة: طلب تشغيل /design-sync بالخطا لجلب التصميم

nodes.label: التدارُك — سحب نظام التصميم كاملًا دفعة وحدة
nodes.rationale: المتدرّب اكتشف مكوّنات ناقصة (جداول وتبويبات وإشعارات ونوافذ تأكيد) وطلب سحب النظام كاملًا؛ التعليمات الآن توجب سحب النظام كاملًا من أوّل مرّة؛ صار النظام 17 مكوّنًا بعد إضافة ستّة ناقصة.
nodes.norm_label: التدارك — سحب نظام التصميم كاملا دفعة وحدة

nodes.label: مراجعة اليوم 7 — جرّب الممنوع لا المسموح فقط
nodes.rationale: مراجعة الصلاحيات لا تكتمل بتجربة ما يعمل بل بتجربة ما يجب أن يُمنع؛ فرّق بين «الصفحة غير موجودة» (لم تُبنَ بعد) و«ما عندك صلاحية» (القيد اشتغل فعلًا) — وحدها الثانية تُحسب.

nodes.label: Claude Design prompt #1 — design system brief
nodes.rationale: Paste-in prompt for a new Design System project: the Arabic RTL-only design system for the SAG Lab bootcamp deck, to be read back into the repo via DesignSync.
nodes.norm_label: claude design prompt #1 — design system brief

nodes.label: Spec of 20 named components (9 frames + 11 elements)
nodes.rationale: Each must be built as a named, reusable component — not 'a set of ready components'.
nodes.norm_label: spec of 20 named components (9 frames + 11 elements)

nodes.label: Per-slide length budget (<=7 bullets, <=90 words, <=8 rows)
nodes.rationale: If content exceeds the budget the design must break it into ١/٢ and ٢/٢ continuation slides — never shrink the type and never allow a scrollbar.
nodes.norm_label: per-slide length budget (<=7 bullets, <=90 words, <=8 rows)

nodes.label: Design System project type is fixed at creation
nodes.rationale: The project type cannot be changed later and only a Design System project can be read back into the repo; a normal project means starting over. Start template 'Color + type pairing' (fallback 'Blank'); never 'Slides' — only the components slides are built from are wanted.
nodes.norm_label: design system project type is fixed at creation

nodes.label: Copy Claude Design form answers back verbatim
nodes.rationale: Claude only knows what is in the prompt; anything decided in Claude Design's question form is invisible and would be assumed noise and dropped at build time unless pasted back into the chat.
nodes.norm_label: copy claude design form answers back verbatim

nodes.label: DesignSync reads the system into the repo (no command)
nodes.rationale: Claude reads the finished components into the repo itself via the DesignSync tool, with no command from the trainer. /design-sync is the opposite direction: it uploads an existing code library to Claude Design, which is not what this is.
nodes.norm_label: designsync reads the system into the repo (no command)

nodes.label: Arabic RTL-only; Latin fragments bidi-wrapped
nodes.rationale: RTL is the default and only direction, not a variant: every component authored dir=rtl, text aligned to start, mirrored layouts. Latin fragments (Claude Code, MVP, MCP, GitHub, Vercel, Supabase, paths, shell commands) sit inline inside Arabic and must be wrapped so a Latin token never flips the line.

nodes.label: CSS logical properties, no left/right in flow
nodes.rationale: margin-inline-start, padding-inline-end, border-inline-start, text-align:start; only genuinely directional things (a forward chevron) may be physical, and they mirror.
nodes.norm_label: css logical properties, no left/right in flow

nodes.label: Fixed 16:9 frame; nothing scrolls inside a slide
nodes.rationale: This is a presentation deck, not a web page: every slide is a fixed 16:9 frame that fits entirely on screen, designed to a fixed height budget.
nodes.norm_label: fixed 16:9 frame; nothing scrolls inside a slide

nodes.label: Self-contained HTML/CSS; only Google Fonts external
nodes.norm_label: self-contained html/css; only google fonts external

nodes.label: Two marks: ساج لاب (lead) and SAG TECH (endorsing)
nodes.rationale: Different marks, not variants. ساج لاب: heavy navy calligraphic two-line Arabic wordmark, no icon, used large on title and divider slides. SAG TECH: circular navy monogram (white spiral reading as S) plus bold Latin caps and Kufi Arabic beneath, used small in the footer as the endorsement.
nodes.norm_label: two marks: ساج لاب (lead) and sag tech (endorsing)

nodes.label: Logo zone: hero / standard / footnote sizes
nodes.rationale: Three sizes with enforced clear-space equal to the monogram's radius; never on a busy background.
nodes.norm_label: logo zone: hero / standard / footnote sizes

nodes.label: Color tokens (primary, deep, sky, snow, ink, teal)
nodes.rationale: --brand-primary #223A71 navy headings and marks; --brand-deep #142447 dark surfaces and cover; --brand-sky #38B6D9 structure (rules, buttons, technical accents); --brand-snow #EEF2F8 cards and sections; --brand-white #FFFFFF; --brand-ink #333B48 body copy; --brand-teal #16C7B7 state only (active step, completed, progress).
nodes.norm_label: color tokens (primary, deep, sky, snow, ink, teal)

nodes.label: Sky = structure, teal = state; never mixed
nodes.rationale: Sky and teal are close in hue, so they must never carry the same meaning on one slide.
nodes.norm_label: sky = structure, teal = state; never mixed

nodes.label: Light default surface + dark surface
nodes.rationale: Light (white/snow, ink text) is the default; dark (--brand-deep, white text, sky accents) is for the title, section dividers and the closing slide.

nodes.label: Type scale sized for the back of the room
nodes.rationale: display 64-72px, slide-title 40-44, section-number 20, body-lead 28-30, body 22-24 (never below 22), caption 18, mono 20 (IBM Plex Mono, forced LTR). Arabic line-height 1.7-1.8 because ascenders and diacritics collide at tighter settings. Projector legibility is the most common failure in decks.
nodes.norm_label: type scale sized for the back of the room

nodes.label: Cairo for Arabic and Latin alike
nodes.rationale: One family for Arabic and the Latin fragments so mixed lines share one skeleton and never shift weight mid-sentence; Cairo is a variable font (200-1000), one file per unicode subset covers every weight; real fallback stack ending in a system Arabic face.
nodes.norm_label: cairo for arabic and latin alike

nodes.label: Layout rules: 5% margins, one idea, media >= 55%
nodes.rationale: Safe margins of at least 5% (projectors crop edges); one idea and one heading per slide (two headings = two slides); media slides give the image >= 55% of the frame and text supports it.
nodes.norm_label: layout rules: 5% margins, one idea, media >= 55%

nodes.label: Visible focus/step highlight state
nodes.rationale: So the presenter can point at one item without any animation.

nodes.label: What not to do: decoration, grey text, animation
nodes.rationale: No stock photography, gradients-as-decoration or shadows heavier than a 2px lift; icons are line, 2px, rounded caps matching the monogram; no light grey text on white (a projector eats contrast); no animation-dependent meaning — the deck must read as static frames.
nodes.norm_label: what not to do: decoration, grey text, animation

nodes.label: Deliverable: tokens, scales, 20 components with states
nodes.rationale: Colour tokens, type scale, spacing scale and the 20 named components, each with states, documented so Claude can read them into the repo via DesignSync.
nodes.norm_label: deliverable: tokens, scales, 20 components with states

nodes.rationale: Header row in --brand-snow.

nodes.label: presenter-block — circular photo + name
nodes.rationale: ~180px photo with a 2px --brand-sky ring on dark surfaces, name and role lines.

nodes.rationale: Links the slide to the curriculum; every content slide carries one — how a trainee finds the slide again in the guide.

nodes.label: media-frame — rounded container for media

nodes.label: step-chip — numbered circle with 3 states
nodes.rationale: upcoming / active (--brand-teal) / done.

nodes.label: file-tree — monospace directory tree
nodes.rationale: Forced LTR (dir=ltr) because box-drawing characters and paths mirror badly under RTL, with Arabic annotations right-aligned beside it.

nodes.label: callout — inline note in three tones
nodes.rationale: Info (sky), warning (amber), rule (teal).

nodes.norm_label: day-progress — which of 10 days is active

nodes.label: Capture rules: filenames, PNG/MP4 not GIF, >=1920x1080, light theme
nodes.rationale: Filenames exact; PNG for a single state, MP4 for any sequence (no audio), never GIF; capture at 1920x1080+ then crop tight; use a clean throwaway account and neutral desktop; never capture a real key/token/password (blur or crop); prefer light OS theme to match the deck's light surfaces.
nodes.norm_label: capture rules: filenames, png/mp4 not gif, >=1920x1080, light theme

nodes.label: Never capture a real key, token or password
nodes.rationale: Bit the project for real once already — see the context7-redacted.mp4 note; blur or crop the value, the slide only needs to show where the button is.

nodes.label: MP4 not GIF — drawImage() on an animated GIF returns frame 0
nodes.rationale: Measured, not assumed: Chromium's drawImage() on an animated GIF returns frame 0 regardless of what's on screen, so a GIF-backed pause button could only ever snap back to its thumbnail. .gifbox now drives a
nodes.norm_label: mp4 not gif — drawimage() on an animated gif returns frame 0

nodes.label: Recordings surfaced undocumented prerequisites
nodes.rationale: Real takes exposed steps no version of the deck or curriculum had documented: the Node.js install gap (github.mp4 shows Claude stalling mid-scaffold), the VS Code 'trust the publisher' prompt, Antigravity's mobile QR verification and possible re-sign-in, and the one-time GitHub Credential Manager 'Authorize' browser step on first push.

nodes.label: context7 key exposure — gblur redaction 0:56-1:46
nodes.rationale: The raw context7.mp4 shows a real, fully readable API key on screen for ~50s (on context7.com's 'key created' modal, then pasted into chat); redacted with ffmpeg's gblur over exactly that window, verified frame-by-frame. The unredacted file still sits in media/ with the key visible — flagged for deletion once the key is confirmed revoked. The Day 3 deployment.mp4 note calls this 'the first recording where a real secret reaches the screen' for production keys, with the same blur-in-post discipline.

nodes.label: git-setup.mp4 — resolution-mismatch reencode
nodes.rationale: Re-shot identity half is 1080p while the original git.mp4 install half is 720p, so -c copy concat is impossible across the resolution change; git.mp4 alone was upscaled once (scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos, x264 CRF 18) and the re-shot clip concatenated in untouched, verified by matching four frames byte-for-byte and by exact frame-count arithmetic (1521+1684=3205).

nodes.label: Verify against extracted frames, not a transcript summary
nodes.rationale: An earlier pass reviewed a recording from an auto-generated summary alone and got real things wrong (misattributed who typed a command, invented a prompt, flagged confirmed facts as unconfirmed) — exactly the mistake the project's own discipline exists to catch; later recordings (Days 4-8) are explicitly frame-verified via ffmpeg trim extraction rather than -ss seek, which was found to mis-time cells via the fps filter's resampling.
nodes.norm_label: verify against extracted frames, not a transcript summary

nodes.label: Do not stage a failure, and do not narrate one that didn't happen
nodes.rationale: d4-2 was planned to capture a genuine first-run skill-trigger miss (per Anthropic's guidance that a description is a guess until tested) but the real second session triggered correctly on an unnamed request, so the slide was built to match that footage and the planned 'fix the description' beat was dropped rather than kept as fiction. The honesty principle cuts both ways.
nodes.norm_label: do not stage a failure, and do not narrate one that didn't happen

nodes.rationale: Entry skill for EVERY touch to a slide (new, one-line fix, restyle, reorder, delete); the description deliberately says no edit is too small to invoke it for.

nodes.label: Self-contained offline RTL slide deck
nodes.rationale: project-package/slides/day-NN.html: no build step, no framework; plain HTML sections, one shared stylesheet, one shared script. Offline because the training room may have no wifi.

nodes.label: Trainees read only the slides
nodes.rationale: Slides ship inside the trainee package next to PRODUCT.md; CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and the curriculum are addressed to Claude. So any trainee-facing content must be on a slide, complete, with no 'see section N of the guide' dependency (CLAUDE.md A.6.1).

nodes.label: project-package (trainee package)
nodes.rationale: Contains slides/, PRODUCT.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and the curriculum; only slides and PRODUCT.md are read by a person.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md (trainee answers file)

nodes.label: Any edit counts: read skill first
