nodes.label: Five things reviews actually fail on
nodes.rationale: Intro says 'hold these four in mind' but five numbered items follow (overflow guard, scaled-unit trap, growing not splitting, commands/output components, stepvid timestamps).
nodes.norm_label: five things reviews actually fail on

nodes.label: Overflow guard is the gate
nodes.rationale: Slide frames are overflow:hidden so excess content is silently clipped and the presenter finds out in the room. deck.js measures every slide; nothing is done until deckAudit prints 'N slides, none overflow'.

nodes.label: Guard measures border boxes, skips inline
nodes.rationale: Cairo's glyph box is taller than its em, so scrollHeight > clientHeight fires on any heading even when nothing is clipped (ink bleed). No amount of splitting clears it. Do not 'fix' the guard to use scrollHeight.
nodes.norm_label: guard measures border boxes, skips inline

nodes.label: Guard cannot see too-empty slides
nodes.rationale: Incident (Day 5): two slides, a bare .flow ordered list and a two-card row, were legal and deckAudit-clean yet used under a third of the frame. Density is invisible to the guard; screenshot every new slide and judge by eye (CLAUDE.md A.6.12).

nodes.label: Scaled-unit trap (divide by --deck-scale)
nodes.rationale: The 1920x1080 frame is transform:scale(--deck-scale): getBoundingClientRect returns scaled device px while getComputedStyle().lineHeight returns unscaled CSS px. Comparing directly once produced a confident '0 wrapped task labels' that one screenshot disproved.

nodes.label: Growing a slide is not splitting it
nodes.rationale: Slide count is a budget. Self-contained means richer cards, a real example, a flow line inside the existing frame; splitting into 1/2 + 2/2 is a last resort and adding a slide is a deliberate requested change (CLAUDE.md A.6.2).
nodes.norm_label: growing a slide is not splitting it

nodes.label: Overflow fixes that have worked
nodes.rationale: Fold an instruction line into a card title; convert a lead paragraph to a compact callout; tighten a gap from --sp-3 to --sp-2; reclaim dead space with align-content: safe center. The 'safe' keyword is load-bearing: plain center overflows both ways, pushing content out through the top where trimming below can never recover it.

nodes.label: Commands and output ride fixed components
nodes.rationale: A trainee must paste a command and recognise output; an inline tok-code span serves neither and gives no copy affordance. Typed/pasted string = full .snipbox with copy button; output = bare .snip without wrapper or button. After any command/output edit grep the slide for tok-code and confirm every hit is a passing mention.
nodes.norm_label: commands and output ride fixed components

nodes.label: Test: does the step ask to reproduce it
nodes.rationale: Not length or how code-like: a single bare word the trainee must find inside a longer list (claude-plugins-official) is still output and gets the bare .snip. Reserve inline tok-code for a short passing mention of a name.
nodes.norm_label: test: does the step ask to reproduce it

nodes.label: Conditional action gets its own step--new row
nodes.rationale: An 'if it isn't listed, add it' branch the recording does not show still gets a full stepvid__step--new row (amber 'مضافة' mark, no data-t) in its correct sequence position, never a parenthetical in the neighbouring step. An omitted data-t is enough for initStepVideos to skip it.
nodes.norm_label: conditional action gets its own step--new row

nodes.label: stepvid timestamps are claims: verify each frame
nodes.rationale: A data-t value asserts 'at this second the recording shows this'; it is true or not, never estimated. Went wrong three times in different ways. Common failure mode: a low-resolution, widely spaced sample (contact sheet, transcript, memory) stands in for the actual frame.
nodes.norm_label: stepvid timestamps are claims: verify each frame

nodes.label: Incident: deployment.mp4 steps from transcript
nodes.rationale: An early pass built the step list from a transcript instead of the video itself.

nodes.label: Incident: slide 9 timing 'completely wrong'
nodes.rationale: tasks-10.3-11.1-11.2.mp4: a pass sampled the video on a fixed 8-second grid and eyeballed thumbnails to place steps. User: 'Your timing is completely wrong!!'. Rebuilt against frames extracted at the user's own corrected timestamps.

nodes.label: Incident: slide 13 seeked PTS labels wrong
nodes.rationale: tasks_12.1_12.2.mp4: sheets built with ffmpeg -ss looked internally consistent and were read with confidence, but the burned-in drawtext times were offset from true time by a drifting amount. Caught only by a deliberate showinfo cross-check.
nodes.norm_label: incident: slide 13 seeked pts labels wrong

nodes.label: ffmpeg -ss silently resets PTS to ~0
nodes.rationale: On this file ffmpeg -ss (before or after -i) resets decoded frames' PTS to ~0 (showinfo pts_time:0 for every non-zero offset). A constant drift looks exactly as consistent as the truth, so a label that looks consistent across a sheet is not evidence.

nodes.label: Use trim=start=X:end=Y instead of -ss
nodes.rationale: trim operates on the normal decoded stream with no seek discontinuity so PTS stay true (verified: trim=start=188:end=192 reported pts_time 188, 188.03...). Never trust a seeked timestamp label without a showinfo or trim cross-check.

nodes.label: Incident: blurry thumbnail misread as wrong-password test
nodes.rationale: Building task-7.11.mp4's step list, a contact-sheet cell looked like a 'test the login with a wrong password' prompt, contradicting the skill's own never-type-a-password rule. A full-resolution frame showed something else entirely; caught only because the check happened before the step was written.
nodes.norm_label: incident: blurry thumbnail misread as wrong-password test

nodes.label: Two passes: coarse sheet, then full frame
nodes.rationale: (1) Coarse pass: contact sheet (tile=NxN at fps=1/N) to find rough shape and approximate seconds. (2) Verification pass: for every timestamp written into data-t, extract that second as a full-resolution single frame (ffmpeg -ss <t> -frames:v 1) and read it before typing the step title. Never promote a coarse guess straight into data-t.
nodes.norm_label: two passes: coarse sheet, then full frame

nodes.label: Writing the Arabic (register rules)
nodes.rationale: Hub for the trainee-facing register rules: pitch level, plain spoken tone, vocabulary, bidi, numerals, و-glue.

nodes.label: Pitch to heard-of-but-unknown level
nodes.rationale: The trainee has heard backend, frontend, server, hosting but not how they work. Give what it is, what it does, when you'd use it, then stop; depth beyond that is Claude's job and costs comprehension on a slide (A.6.4).

nodes.label: Plain, spoken, never compressed
nodes.rationale: Write it the way you'd say it aloud, short sentences. Telegraphic phrasing where each word carries a paragraph reads as obfuscated, not concise; canonical bad example «تطبيق، فعملك، فمراجعة» (A.6.3).

nodes.label: A rule must name its applying test
nodes.rationale: Never compressed is not only register: slide 11's addition rule «إن خدم شاشة موجودة فأضِفه قسمًا لها…» never said how to tell if something 'serves' an existing screen; the missing test was: does it open at its own URL or just add to an existing screen? Read a sentence back and ask 'could I apply this to a new case right now' (A.6.13).
nodes.norm_label: a rule must name its applying test

nodes.label: Never heavily dialectal (المحكية البيضاء)
nodes.rationale: The other edge, which reviews keep catching: lean colloquial but use spoken words any Arabic reader parses, not Gulf-only. يقدّم/يعمل/ينفّذ not يسوّي; ايش not وش; يحتاج/يبي not يبغى; «كل ما احتجت» not «وقت ما التبس». Colloquial connectives (اللي، عشان، بس، مو) stay; dialect verbs shut non-Gulf readers out.

nodes.label: Never open a row or title with a و-word
nodes.rationale: Includes «وايش» and «ووين»; they read as a fragment continuing something that isn't there. Mid-sentence the same words are fine.
nodes.norm_label: never open a row or title with a و-word

nodes.label: One trainee, singular, always
nodes.rationale: Each trainee builds alone. A plural reads as 'me and the other trainees' or 'me and Claude', and Claude is a tool the trainee operates. Never «تشتغلون/وصلتم/توصلون/أنتم/سوا» with Claude as the other party; say «في كل مهمّة عليك شغل، وعلى Claude شغل». Exception: trainer plus room in a live session («ننجزها معًا الآن», §7.10). (A.6.7.1)

nodes.label: Concrete examples only
nodes.rationale: «لو عندك متجر وتبغى تعرف كم طلب وصلك اليوم» beats «مثال على استعلام البيانات». If an example can't be made concrete it isn't understood well enough to teach (A.6.5).

nodes.label: Example assuming unestablished domain is borrowed scenery
nodes.rationale: Incident: a Day-2 slide explained role overlap with «مقدّم الخدمة حجز مواعيده الخاصّة», vivid only if you already hold a booking domain the deck never set up. Test: could a trainee who read only this deck, to this slide, picture it? Prefer the example that day's own recording is about to play: no setup cost, pays twice.
nodes.norm_label: example assuming unestablished domain is borrowed scenery

nodes.label: Calibrate how much rides on the example
nodes.rationale: Examples beat abstraction but the dose is a judgement. Test: could the trainee understand the definition cold? Then clarifying; if the definition would land as noise first, gateway. Most topics do not clear the gateway bar; over-dosing a light topic buys nothing (CLAUDE.md A.6.11).
nodes.norm_label: calibrate how much rides on the example

nodes.label: Clarifying example (default dose)
nodes.rationale: One line, one card, a real number, inside the explanation.

nodes.label: Gateway example (rare, deliberate)
nodes.rationale: For heavy/technical topics: open on a situation the trainee already lives, walk it as a sequence, never name the concept while the story runs, reveal in the closing line, then explain on the next slide by pointing back at it. Earns a whole slide.

nodes.label: §7.5 MCP: the worked gateway case
nodes.rationale: Slide 24 is the Gmail story with MCP unnamed until its last line; slide 25 names the parts by reflecting them back onto it. A gateway's badge and title can spoil its own reveal, so slide 24's badge had to change too.

nodes.label: Show the flow before the work
nodes.rationale: Never drop trainees into steps without saying plainly what the sequence is for and in what order. Medium-neutral: some framings belong on a slide, others are just something the trainer says; decide per case and say which (A.6.6).
nodes.norm_label: show the flow before the work

nodes.label: Verb person matters (ن- vs ت-)
nodes.rationale: «ن-» verbs mean we do this together: right for «تطبيق مع المدرب», wrong for «مراجعة وعرض التقدم» and for anything the trainee does alone. Incident: «نجهّز جهازك» when the trainer only demonstrates promises something the session does not keep.

nodes.label: Fixed vocabulary table
nodes.rationale: Hub for the choices that never vary on trainee-facing text (CLAUDE.md A.6.7).

nodes.label: مشروع not منتج
nodes.rationale: Trainees build projects, not products.

nodes.label: الدورة / القسم N / الحزمة, never دليل
nodes.rationale: The deck is the curriculum; there is no separate guide.
nodes.norm_label: الدورة / القسم n / الحزمة, never دليل

nodes.label: منهج means curriculum (not محتوى)
nodes.rationale: Use منهج where curriculum is meant, never محتوى.

nodes.label: محتوى الملفات / فهرس المحتويات, never منهج
nodes.rationale: These are file contents and a table of contents.
nodes.norm_label: محتوى الملفات / فهرس المحتويات, never منهج

nodes.label: ايش, never وش/ويش/ووش
nodes.rationale: The colloquial 'what' is ايش; the و is a separate conjunction, not part of it. وايش is wrong as the default.

nodes.label: يقدّم/يعمل/ينفّذ, never يسوّي
nodes.rationale: Gulf-only verb; the register stays spoken without it.

nodes.label: سطر الأوامر / موجّه الأوامر, never الطرفية
nodes.rationale: سطر الأوامر for the concept, موجّه الأوامر for a window you open, Terminal/PowerShell for a named program. الطرفية reads as stilted; hand-corrected out of the deck repeatedly before the rule was written down.
nodes.norm_label: سطر الاوامر / موجه الاوامر, never الطرفية

nodes.label: مجموعة شرائح, never بلوك
nodes.rationale: No English words spelled in Arabic letters.

nodes.label: ملفات تشغيل الشرائح, never ما يخصّك
nodes.rationale: Never phrase something as beneath the trainee.
nodes.norm_label: ملفات تشغيل الشرايح, never ما يخصك

nodes.label: خصائص, never مجالات/نقاط/عناصر نطاق
nodes.rationale: The scope list is خصائص derived from غايات; the terminology box bans every synonym.

nodes.label: مشروع الأولي (except MVP phrase)
nodes.rationale: منتج survives only as the P in «المنتج التقني الأولي (MVP)» and in the programme's own name.

nodes.label: ربط until §7.5 defines التكامل
nodes.rationale: Never التكاملات before slide 23; ربط is plainer and the noun is not introduced yet.

nodes.label: موعد / مواعيد متاحة, never التوفّر
nodes.rationale: Use موعد, مواعيد متاحة, يفتح مواعيد دفعة وحدة instead of التوفّر and التوليد الجماعي.

nodes.label: Concrete noun beats nominalisation
nodes.rationale: التوفّر and التوليد الجماعي are nominalisations the trainee must unpack before the sentence means anything; مواعيد متاحة needs no unpacking. The tell is a تفعّل/تفعيل-pattern noun where a plain one exists. Reported on Day-2 slide 12, 2026-09-25.

nodes.label: Terminology sweeps are semantic, never sed
nodes.rationale: Read every candidate in place. Incident: a blind swap on «صمّم محتوى الدورة ومنهجه» yields «صمّم منهج الدورة ومنهجه».
nodes.norm_label: terminology sweeps are semantic, never sed

nodes.label: ايش is و+ايش: audit /وايش/
nodes.rationale: Write ايش unless a conjunction is genuinely needed (a list «مين هو، وايش دوره، ووين وصلتم» or two joined clauses). After an em-dash, a colon, or at the start of a title/clause there is nothing to join, so the و is wrong. Read every hit; the correct count is small.

nodes.label: Never label a task by who performs it
nodes.rationale: The trainee works on all 29 tasks; the source column «مَن ينفّذها» needed a footnote to stop it reading as 'I am not involved in nineteen of these', the tell it was wrong. Deck says «دورك فيها» and names a trainee action per row: تقرّر وتوصف (10), تراجع وتصحّح (7), تجرّب وتعدّل (12).
nodes.norm_label: never label a task by who performs it

nodes.label: تكامل (the thing) vs ربط (the act)
nodes.rationale: Not synonyms; do not unify. تكامل is the subject of §7.5's title (an MCP connection), ربط is connecting one. Ordering rule: a slide before §7.5 must say ربط الأدوات الخارجية since التكاملات would be undefined to a cold reader.

nodes.label: Every task row opens with a verb
nodes.rationale: «المشكلة والهدف والغايات» is a label; «تحديد المشكلة والهدف والغايات» is a task. A vague row is rewritten to name its output: «بقيّة أصحاب المصلحة» became «تحديد الخدمات الخارجية والأطراف المتأثّرة بمشروعك».
nodes.norm_label: every task row opens with a verb

nodes.label: Title states the takeaway, spoken Arabic
nodes.rationale: Compressed فصحى titles are a register failure: «حدّان يتجدّدان — لا رصيد لا نهائي» became «رصيدك يتجدّد لحاله، بس فيه حدّين لازم تعرفهم». A title must still describe the slide after it changes; two went stale unnoticed.
nodes.norm_label: title states the takeaway, spoken arabic

nodes.label: ؟ window belongs on the slide that uses the term
nodes.rationale: Incident: defining «كيان» on a Day-2 slide whose cards only said «الدور» was reported as actively confusing: the trainee hunts the slide for the word and doesn't find it. Grep the slide for the term before shipping a ؟; if absent move it and rewrite the sentence to introduce the idea.
nodes.norm_label: ؟ window belongs on the slide that uses the term

nodes.label: Never use a term before its defining slide
nodes.rationale: «التكاملات» appeared 15 slides before §7.5 defined it; «متطلّب» belongs to §10 and must not leak into §8. If genuinely needed earlier, reorder rather than define twice.
nodes.norm_label: never use a term before its defining slide

nodes.label: No invented quantitative anchors
nodes.rationale: «45 رسالة قصيرة» was fabricated. If a number can't be sourced delete it and record why so it can't drift back. Prefer a measurable anchor (a 300-line file ≈ 4k tokens) over a rate.

nodes.label: Bidi: mechanical rules
nodes.rationale: Heading says 'four mechanical rules' but five bullets follow (the dimension-pair rule was added later).

nodes.label: End an Arabic sentence with an Arabic word
nodes.rationale: A sentence ending in a Latin word puts the full stop at the wrong end (`. read_email`).
nodes.norm_label: end an arabic sentence with an arabic word

nodes.label: Neutral char after isolated Latin jumps
nodes.rationale: A neutral character after an isolated Latin run jumps to the other end; reorder so the Latin token lands last in its clause.
nodes.norm_label: neutral char after isolated latin jumps

nodes.label: Never chain A ← B inside one tok-lat
nodes.rationale: It reads left-to-right and reverses the order for an Arabic reader. Use two elements joined by an Arabic verb: «افتح Settings ثم اختر Usage». An arrow cannot fix this; a verb can.
nodes.norm_label: never chain a ← b inside one tok-lat

nodes.label: LTR number box glues to Arabic in RTL cell
nodes.rationale: «8.1المشكلة» needs text-align: end and a min-width.
nodes.norm_label: ltr number box glues to arabic in rtl cell

nodes.label: Dimension pair with × flips in Arabic text
nodes.rationale: «1200×630» between two Arabic runs renders backwards even with plain Latin digits; an isolating span does not reliably fix it. Say it in words: «عرضها 1200 وارتفاعها 630». Same for any A×B-shaped token.
nodes.norm_label: dimension pair with × flips in arabic text

nodes.label: Latin digits only, never ١٢٣
nodes.rationale: Mixed scripts read as inconsistent and Arabic-Indic digits reorder unpredictably beside Latin tokens in RTL. Audit /[٠-٩]/. Found on Day 1 and Day 2 stage__n badges and Day 3 EARS card ordinals as of 2026-09-29; fix on next touch, not proactively.

nodes.label: Never glue Arabic و to a Latin word
nodes.rationale: `وpush` / `وSupabase` render as one run and read as a typo. Use & when the و joins two Latin tokens that pair (commit & push), or a space (و Supabase) for an ordinary conjunction. Audit /و(?:<[^>]+>)*[A-Za-z]/ over the HTML and over rendered text, since the markup form misses cases that glue only after tags are stripped.
nodes.norm_label: never glue arabic و to a latin word

nodes.label: Four sessions per day
nodes.rationale: شرح المفاهيم, تطبيق مع المدرب, عملك على مشروعك, مراجعة وعرض التقدم.

nodes.label: Days 2-10 carry two session-break slides
nodes.rationale: From Day 2 the first two sessions are one interleaved block, so only «عملك على مشروعك» and «مراجعة وعرض التقدم» open with a break slide; the first doesn't either, since the day opens on شرح المفاهيم. Without breaks a trainee can't tell the session changed. Day 1 keeps three because its «تطبيق مع المدرب» is a separate device-setup walkthrough; do not 'fix' it down to two.

nodes.label: Break slide: full-bleed sag-quote frame
nodes.rationale: sag-slide sag-quote deck-slide, data-tone=rule, data-surface=dark; footer carries only the session badge (no logo, no day label). The only legitimate sag-quote use that is not a real pull-quote.

nodes.label: «ticking tasks is your job» attr line
nodes.rationale: The __attr line says what the session needs and nothing else covers; the عملك على مشروعك break tells the trainee that ticking finished tasks is their job.
nodes.norm_label: «ticking tasks is your job» attr line

nodes.label: Task rows: keys, nesting, cross-slide sync
nodes.rationale: .task rows are checkboxes (A.6.9). data-task-key = explicit id, data-parent = the key it rolls up into, task--l2/l3 = indentation. Markup stays a FLAT list; nesting .task elements would break the .tasks flex column and the .task grid.
nodes.norm_label: task rows: keys, nesting, cross-slide sync

nodes.label: Same data-task-key repaints everywhere
nodes.rationale: Day-plan slide lists «7.10 · تجهّز جهازك أنت» as one line while the work slide breaks it into eleven rows; ticking either moves both. Parent/child maps are built over keys, so a parent ticked on one slide cascades into children on another. A parent shows partial (dash) until a full house; clicking a partial parent fills it in.

nodes.label: Give syncing rows an explicit data-task-key
nodes.rationale: Matching on label text across slides is brittle: a ؟ qmark button's text is part of the label, so identical-looking rows aren't identical. Adding a key orphans whatever was stored under the old label-derived key; harmless between cohorts.
nodes.norm_label: give syncing rows an explicit data-task-key

nodes.label: Look-alike rows can be different tasks
nodes.rationale: Day 1 has «7.10 · نستعرض خطوات تجهيز الجهاز أمامك» (trainer demos) and «7.10 · تجهّز جهازك أنت» (trainee does it): same section, two tasks, two keys, never merge.
nodes.norm_label: look-alike rows can be different tasks

nodes.label: Task rows assume a light surface
nodes.rationale: [data-done=true] paints a pale teal that white --text-heading would vanish into. Put the checklist on a light slide and let the break slide before it carry the dark.
nodes.norm_label: task rows assume a light surface

nodes.label: Three surfaces must stay in sync
nodes.rationale: A wording change usually lives in more than one file; after any content edit grep all of them and report what you found.
nodes.norm_label: three surfaces must stay in sync

nodes.label: project-package/slides/day-NN.html
nodes.rationale: The slides, including the <!-- ═══ N — title ═══ --> banner above each one.

nodes.label: bootcamp_roadmap_and_curriculum.md
nodes.rationale: The authoring source. Headings own GitHub anchors, so renaming a heading breaks every link unless the TOC entry and every cross-reference move with it.

nodes.label: deck/ per-day briefs (DECK_BRIEF, day-NN-brief)
nodes.rationale: DECK_BRIEF.md is Day 1's (named before the convention existed), then day-02-brief.md and so on. All carry slide numbers that go stale when a slide is inserted.

nodes.label: deck/MEDIA_SHOTLIST.md
nodes.rationale: Covers every day, not just Day 1; after the 2026-09-25 showcase reversal days 2-10 got recordings of their own, each a section including shots not yet filmed (marked ⬜). deck/ holds only these planning docs.

nodes.label: The .docx curriculum mirror is retired
nodes.rationale: bootcamp_roadmap_and_curriculum.docx was a hand-edited Word mirror, painful to patch; trainees never read it. It sits in archive/ and is not maintained: do not edit it or re-add it to the sync list.

nodes.label: Footer numbers written by deck.js
nodes.rationale: Inserting a slide does not mean touching dozens of spans; the day label (.deck-foot__side .deck-foot__num) is hand-authored. DECK_BRIEF and MEDIA_SHOTLIST carry hand-written numbers: renumber bottom-up (top-down collides) and assert each row matches exactly once before replacing.

nodes.label: Verification checklist (report each result)
nodes.rationale: Run all and report each result rather than asserting success: deckAudit on the real page via chrome-devtools, screenshots, qmark grep, interactive behaviours, register sweeps, curriculum prompt count, term windows, commands as snipbox, break-slide count, checkbox hierarchy, anchors, offline.

nodes.label: Register sweep by verb family
nodes.rationale: Sweep يسو/تسو/نسو/سوّ, not one spelling. Incident: a clean single-spelling grep passed a «تسوي» written minutes earlier; the family sweep's first real run found three more on Day 1. Exclude the noun «المسوّدة»; read the rest in place.

nodes.label: .docx structure check item (stale?)
nodes.rationale: The checklist still lists '.docx structure: counts unchanged, TOC anchors resolve, jc=right = 0, 14 of 15 zip entries byte-identical' although the .docx is retired and not maintained.

nodes.label: Offline: no remote font/script/image
nodes.rationale: The training room may have no wifi, and a deck that loses its icons on stage is a failed deck.

nodes.label: Working method: gradual, few slides at a time
nodes.rationale: Fix THAT slide against everything above, leave the rest, then say which slides most need the same treatment next. The closing recommendation is part of the deliverable (A.6.10).
nodes.norm_label: working method: gradual, few slides at a time

nodes.label: Reported defect is a sample, not the bug
nodes.rationale: Named one badly-styled slide, five more had the same fault; named three bad task rows, eleven were wrong. Fix the instance, enumerate the whole class, report both counts (how many checked, how many found).
nodes.norm_label: reported defect is a sample, not the bug

nodes.label: Verification scope tracks edit scope
nodes.rationale: deckAudit and deckRefAudit are whole-deck and free, so always run them. Full text sweeps are for deck-wide changes only (terminology unification, new styling rule, deck.css edit). Opening every reply with a 50-slide verification after touching one slide was called out as waste.

nodes.label: New styling rule earns one deck-wide sweep
nodes.rationale: The rule is new, so nothing before it was built to comply. Then record what deliberately stays as-is so the next sweep does not re-flag it.
nodes.norm_label: new styling rule earns one deck-wide sweep

nodes.label: Redundant content is deleted, not reworded
nodes.rationale: When told something is already covered elsewhere, delete it rather than rescue it with a rewrite and a distinction. Then fix the grid's data-cols and hunt orphaned sentences that referenced it.
nodes.norm_label: redundant content is deleted, not reworded

nodes.label: Bump banner numbers before inserting
nodes.rationale: Renumber every <!-- ═══ N — … --> at or above the insertion point first, then splice the new slide in with its own banner; the other way round catches the new banner in the same pass. Back up before the splice; deletions are the mirror operation.

nodes.label: Validate the validator
nodes.rationale: Before trusting a custom audit script, prove it fails on deliberately broken input. Incident: one reported 55 phantom broken links because its slug rules didn't match GitHub's; the real count was zero.

nodes.label: ffmpeg exit code 0 is not success
nodes.rationale: Verify by duration, frame count or pixel comparison. A mangled path once produced a silently truncated file at exit 0, and a bad flag produced two empty frames that compared as 'identical'.
nodes.norm_label: ffmpeg exit code 0 is not success

nodes.label: 'Leave it alone' decisions are scoped
nodes.rationale: The handout was deliberately left stale for three days because reconciling it sat outside that session's scope; a later session explicitly asked to reconcile it and did. That is a new in-scope decision superseding an old out-of-scope one, not a reversal. Read an old note for the scope it was made under.

nodes.label: Reversed rule needs its trigger restated
nodes.rationale: 'Every screen needs an origin' kept its wording across a reshape but flipped meaning: once Claude extracts first, it is dead weight unless re-scoped to screens the trainee adds. The same mistake shipped again one turn later inside the fix. Ask what has actually happened by this step, not whether it matches what you already know to avoid.
nodes.norm_label: reversed rule needs its trigger restated

nodes.label: Reviewing AI output is not stating what only the trainee knows
nodes.rationale: A review-structure reshape (passes, gap list, origin field) can improve a task while staying entirely about checking Claude's work; nothing asks the trainee to say what was never in the source data. When a task's purpose is 'trainee input matters', check for an actual elicitation prompt, not a count of review steps.
nodes.norm_label: reviewing ai output is not stating what only the trainee knows

nodes.label: A list for later is not acting on it now

nodes.rationale: A 2026-09-25 note claimed 'no BookIt material survives in any deck'; it was wrong and unchecked for two weeks. A full audit found six BookIt-vocabulary sites across days 1, 2, 6, 7, 8. Do not trust a blanket 'it's all gone' claim; grep for the nouns.

nodes.label: day-08 slide 7 opened «في المهمة 14.3»
nodes.rationale: The worst unframed case: it reads as the task the trainee did yesterday on their own project.

nodes.label: Disposition: frame it
nodes.rationale: Use when the incident IS the domain (e.g. a provider could book their own slot). Open with «في مشروع سابق للمدرب — نظام حجز مواعيد، مو اللي في المقاطع», then use the nouns freely. Put it in the slide's lead so the cards inherit it; drop into the card only when the lead is occupied.

nodes.label: Disposition: genericise it
nodes.rationale: Use when the lesson is domain-free and understanding the example costs two or three prerequisite facts: strip the nouns. The «لماذا لا…؟» filter story became «تصفية بحسب من يقدّمها», same lesson with zero prerequisites.

nodes.label: Frame at earliest occurrence, call back later

nodes.label: .card (the workhorse)

Block flow, not flex. A warning card has no modifier, only an inline border-inline-start:5px solid var(--state-warning).

nodes.label: .stat

nodes.label: .sess (one session column)

nodes.label: Use sess__note--foot under a task list

nodes.norm_label: use sess__note--foot under a task list

nodes.label: .task / .tasks live checkboxes
nodes.rationale: Flat sibling rows. data-task-key = cross-slide identity, data-parent = roll-up by key never by DOM nesting, task--l2/l3 indent, tasks--tree 6px gap, task--free dashed, data-done=partial set by JS only. Without a key the row is identified by its .task__t text, so rewording resets saved state. Assumes a light surface.

nodes.label: .stepvid (recording + timed steps)
nodes.rationale: Video first in markup (lands visually RIGHT under RTL) + ordered step list; steps carry data-t and a stepvid__time button. .stepvid__list is a sanctioned scroller. __player and __list are required class names: initStepVideos bails without them.

nodes.label: Amber means the list is right, the recording behind
nodes.rationale: All amber affordances use the same colour on purpose so the trainee learns one rule.
nodes.norm_label: amber means the list is right, the recording behind

nodes.label: stepvid__step--new

nodes.label: stepvid__fix
nodes.rationale: For an on-screen step whose content moved: an amber inset note inside __body (`مو في المقطع:`).

nodes.label: stepvid__mark--idx
nodes.rationale: For a step with no matching video moment: a sky ordinal badge instead of a dead 0:00 button.

nodes.label: stepvid__video--soon + stepvid__soon
nodes.rationale: For a capture that does not exist yet: a dashed placeholder box.

nodes.label: Omit data-t to author a non-video row
nodes.rationale: parseFloat(null) is NaN, which initStepVideos already skips on both click and highlight paths; no JS change needed. Once the footage matches, DELETE the amber note, do not convert it.
nodes.norm_label: omit data-t to author a non-video row

nodes.label: initStepVideos()
nodes.rationale: Wires timed steps to the video; bails without .stepvid__player and .stepvid__list; skips steps whose data-t is NaN.

nodes.label: .snipbox (command + copy button)
nodes.rationale: cmd

nodes.label: Bare .snip (output, no wrapper/button)
nodes.rationale: Output the trainee reads and matches against but never copies.

nodes.label: Test: does the step ask to reproduce this string
nodes.rationale: Not length, not how code-like it looks. A single bare word they must find in a longer list is still output. Inline tok-code is only for a passing mention.
nodes.norm_label: test: does the step ask to reproduce this string

nodes.label: Inline tok-code span
nodes.rationale: Reserved for a short passing mention of a name, never a string the step asks the trainee to type or locate.

nodes.label: .promptbox (prepared prompt for Claude)
nodes.rationale: A copy button with data-copy plus a visible paragraph carrying the SAME wording (update both together or they drift). Use wherever a step's point is 'copy this and paste it to Claude'; not a .snipbox (short command) nor a card--plain quote (no copy affordance). Real instances: day-05 slides task-121 and task-121-gap.

nodes.label: Prompt names where data lives, not which task
nodes.rationale: By the time a prompt runs, the data is already in PRODUCT.md (the current state). Pointing at a task number («من رحلتي (11.1)») makes Claude reconstruct from a finished process; point at the section: «القسم 4 في PRODUCT.md». Caught on Day 5: slide 8's extraction prompt shipped with the task-number version.
nodes.norm_label: prompt names where data lives, not which task

nodes.label: A numbered-task prompt must OPEN with the task number
nodes.rationale: «طبّق مهمّة 14.5: …». Claude reads the prompt with the whole building-features/SKILL.md available but cannot tell which of its seven task sections is invoked; the number selects the right one (inputs, steps, completion check). Incident: Day 8's 14.5 prompt shipped without it while 14.3's and 14.4's had it.
nodes.norm_label: a numbered-task prompt must open with the task number

nodes.label: The two prompt rules compose, not conflict
nodes.rationale: They govern different halves: the leading task number names WHAT to run; body references name WHERE data is. One prompt carries both: «طبّق مهمّة 14.5: … كما وصفتها في رحلتي (القسم 4 في PRODUCT.md)».
nodes.norm_label: the two prompt rules compose, not conflict

nodes.label: Gap and hygiene prompts take no task number
nodes.rationale: Applies to a prompt invoking a numbered task, not every .promptbox: a gap prompt («فكّرت في [شاشة] ما ذكرتها…») or session-hygiene prompt belongs to no task; a number would be a false claim.
nodes.norm_label: gap and hygiene prompts take no task number

nodes.label: Exception: no section exists yet to point at
nodes.rationale: A prompt for the task that first produces a PRODUCT.md section has nothing to reference. 'تعتمد على المهمة 11.1' in task metadata is sequencing information, not an instruction on where to pull data from.
nodes.norm_label: exception: no section exists yet to point at

nodes.label: Media frame (image / plain video)
nodes.rationale: sag-media-frame with a box, a video and a caption plus a sag-media__side card. Only instance: day-01.html:2219-2252.

nodes.label: .flow (+ --row) numbered sequence
nodes.rationale: Numbered via CSS counter on a bare <ol>. For ordered steps; .bento reads as parallel facts. Copy: day-01.html:1818-1824, 2082-2087.

nodes.label: .agenda (--break, --main)
nodes.rationale: Day-rhythm rows (day-01.html:174-193).

nodes.label: .idx (data-group)
nodes.rationale: Index cell; .idx__t is one line, ellipsised (733-760).

nodes.label: .pkgtree
nodes.rationale: The package listing (__p, __d, --read, --mute); a sanctioned scroller (1099-1180).

nodes.label: .tmap (29-task table)
nodes.rationale: Lives inside a <template class=terms> and needs data-wide=true; badges __b--decide / review / try (536-711).

nodes.label: .dlbtn download button
nodes.rationale: A real download link styled as a button; must be an <a href> (2232).

nodes.label: .deck-part '1 / 2' marker
nodes.rationale: Inline inside the <h2> (907).

nodes.label: .sag-slide__lead--wide
nodes.rationale: Lifts the 34ch cap on that slide only; for a definition, not a hook.

nodes.label: .sag-slide__title--note
nodes.rationale: Inline commentary span inside the <h2> (1094).

nodes.label: .kbd keycap
nodes.rationale: Light background, not for dark slides (1964).

nodes.label: Interaction layer: three affordances, one engine
nodes.rationale: Choose: one short clause on a phrase -> .ttip[data-tip]; one short definition on a term/acronym -> .ttip--icon; a paragraph or several related terms -> .qmark + <template class=terms>.
nodes.norm_label: interaction layer: three affordances, one engine

nodes.label: Legend slide (data-anchor=legend)
nodes.rationale: Teaches the affordances to trainees with live demos; add any new affordance there too or nobody will find it.

nodes.label: .ttip[data-tip]
nodes.rationale: One short clause on a phrase.

nodes.label: .ttip--icon (term / acronym)
nodes.rationale: Needs data-tip-title and data-tip. .i is a CSS mask and renders nothing but the mask, so anything nested inside an .i is invisible: the entire reason .ttip--icon exists as a wrapper.

nodes.label: .qmark + terms template
nodes.rationale: <button class=qmark type=button data-term=...>؟</button> opens a panel from the slide's <template class=terms>. The ؟ is a literal Arabic character, not an icon (icons.css has none, and a mirrored Latin ? is wrong in RTL).

nodes.label: <template class=terms>
nodes.rationale: One per slide, anywhere inside the section. Opening any ؟ renders ALL that slide's terms with the clicked one highlighted (suppressed when only one). data-wide=true widens to 1320px for a table. Inner HTML injected verbatim.

nodes.label: qmark button holds only the ؟ glyph
nodes.rationale: <button class=qmark>مكوّنات؟</button> renders the whole word inside the small circular badge and collides with the text below. The word stays plain text immediately before the button. Caught only by screenshot since deckAudit checks overflow, not malformed components; grep each new qmark for more than one character.
nodes.norm_label: qmark button holds only the ؟ glyph

nodes.label: A reusable .qmark is often the right fix
nodes.rationale: A plain-language ask like 'an icon that explains RTL and LTR' describes an interaction (click a marker, see a definition) that .qmark + terms template already does. Check it before inventing a second mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: a reusable .qmark is often the right fix

nodes.label: data-ref deep link + section name
nodes.rationale: On a .task, .reflink or card. deck.js resolves it against this deck and builds the tooltip from the target slide's own badge, so a rename cannot desync it. Resolution order: data-anchor equals ref; badge number equals ref; badge label contains ref. First match wins, so two slides sharing a badge number both resolve to the earlier: give the later a data-anchor. Anchor names may be Arabic. Ctrl/Cmd+click jumps, Backspace returns.

nodes.label: .reflink live cross-reference
nodes.rationale: Any cross-reference to another slide is a live reflink, never prose; «بعد البند 5» is a defect.

nodes.label: data-ref cannot cross day files
nodes.rationale: resolveRef searches only the current document. A Day-2 slide cannot link to Day 1's mvp-scope; anything a later day needs must be restated briefly in that day's own deck.

nodes.label: window.deckRefAudit()
nodes.rationale: Returns unresolved data-ref values and fails loudly on a dead ref; also proves no ref points at a Day-1 anchor missing from this file.

nodes.label: Closed set of 22 icons
nodes.rationale: i-alert-triangle, book-open, calendar, check, circle-check, clock, cloud-upload, copy, database, download, file-text, git-branch, info, layers, lightbulb, list-checks, palette, rocket, shield-check, terminal, users, wrench. There is no question-mark icon and no dash icon (the partial-task dash is an inline --i override in deck.css).

nodes.label: Design tokens (semantic aliases)
nodes.rationale: Colour tokens are semantic aliases over a 7-colour palette. Reference the alias, never raw --brand-*, or a dark slide will not flip.

nodes.label: Sky = structure, teal = state only
nodes.rationale: --accent-structure (sky) is for rules, buttons, technical accents; --accent-state (teal) is for active/done/progress only.

nodes.label: Effective type scale
nodes.rationale: After deck.css:333-340 raises defaults: --fs-display 76px, --fs-slide-title 46, --fs-body-lead 33, --fs-body 26, --fs-caption 24, --fs-mono 20.

nodes.label: Never override a font size downward to fit
nodes.rationale: Split the slide instead; the floor may only ever be raised.
nodes.norm_label: never override a font size downward to fit

nodes.label: Spacing, radii, elevation tokens
nodes.rationale: --sp-1..8 = 8/16/24/32/48/64/96/128; --radius-sm|md|lg|pill = 8/14/24/999; max elevation 2px (--lift-1, --lift-2, --lift-2-dark); border --border-hairline.

nodes.label: data-surface=dark remaps tokens
nodes.rationale: Remaps --surface-slide, --surface-card (#1B2E56), --surface-card-line, --text-heading (white), --text-body, --text-caption, --text-link, --rule-hairline.

nodes.label: --deck-scale and --tip-dx runtime vars
nodes.rationale: Set by JS: --deck-scale on <html>, --tip-dx on each .tip.

nodes.label: deck.js contract
nodes.rationale: Exports and behaviours the deck depends on: audits, navigation keys, footer numbering, task state, HUD (idle-hides after 2s so it never covers content), init order.

nodes.label: window.deckAudit()
nodes.rationale: Logs and returns the overflowing slide numbers. THE gate: nothing is done until it prints 'N slides, none overflow'. Measures border boxes and skips inline boxes.

nodes.label: Navigation keys (RTL)
nodes.rationale: Arrow/Space/PageUp/PageDown navigate (RTL: ArrowLeft advances); Home/End/F/H = first/last/fullscreen/hide HUD; Backspace undoes the last deep-link jump.

nodes.label: Task state in localStorage per day file
nodes.rationale: Key sag-deck:<filename>:tasks, namespaced per day file so keys never collide across days.
nodes.norm_label: task state in localstorage per day file

nodes.label: Init order is deliberate
nodes.rationale: initGifs, initRefs, initTips, initQmarks, initTasks, initCopyButtons, initStepVideos. initRefs runs BEFORE initTasks so a task row's Ctrl-check is bound ahead of its checkbox toggle.

nodes.label: initGifs()
nodes.rationale: First step of the init sequence.

nodes.label: initRefs()
nodes.rationale: Resolves data-ref values; must run before initTasks.

nodes.label: initTips()
nodes.rationale: Wires .ttip tooltips.

nodes.label: initQmarks()
nodes.rationale: Wires .qmark term windows.

nodes.label: initTasks()
nodes.rationale: Builds byKey / childrenOf / parentOf over KEYS, not elements, which makes one key repaint on every slide it appears on. Parent states true / 'partial' / false are recomputed from children at load rather than trusted from storage.

nodes.label: initCopyButtons()
nodes.rationale: Handles .snipbox__copy and .promptbox__copy; relies on the execCommand fallback because navigator.clipboard rejects under file://.

nodes.label: Traps that have actually bitten
nodes.rationale: Three groups: layout and measurement, markup that silently breaks, environment.

nodes.label: transform: scale() does not shrink layout box
nodes.rationale: getBoundingClientRect is scaled device px; divide by --deck-scale before comparing to a CSS px value.
nodes.norm_label: transform: scale() does not shrink layout box

nodes.label: Guard measures border boxes, skips inline
nodes.rationale: Cairo's glyph box is taller than its em, so scrollHeight > clientHeight on any heading even when nothing is clipped (ink bleed). Do not 'fix' the guard to use scrollHeight.
nodes.norm_label: guard measures border boxes, skips inline

nodes.label: Do not hand-roll an overflow diagnostic
nodes.rationale: One ad-hoc script blamed .tip overlays for 52px when the real culprit was a card__note 2.9px over: it failed to replicate boxOverflow's rejection of absolutely-positioned subtrees. Run deckAudit() or copy the walker faithfully.
nodes.norm_label: do not hand-roll an overflow diagnostic

nodes.label: align-content: safe center, safe is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Plain center overflows equally in both directions, pushing content out through the top where trimming below can never recover it.
nodes.norm_label: align-content: safe center, safe is load-bearing

nodes.label: .card must not be a flex column
nodes.rationale: Margins do not collapse in flex, so every extra .card__note cost the gap plus ~18px above plus ~18px below.
nodes.norm_label: .card must not be a flex column

nodes.label: .card > * does not reach grandchildren
nodes.rationale: An <h3> inside .card__top kept its UA margin 1em 0: 41 dead px in every card in the deck until zeroed.

nodes.label: Horizontal overflow is a separate check
nodes.rationale: deckAudit does not cover it; watch .snip boxes and step lists, including inside ؟ windows.
nodes.norm_label: horizontal overflow is a separate check

nodes.label: overflow-wrap: anywhere, not break-word
nodes.rationale: Only 'anywhere' shrinks min-content so a box can actually contract around long tokens.

nodes.label: A real <video> inflates its box
nodes.rationale: Force it absolute inside .sag-media-frame__box.

nodes.label: Reclaim space before cutting words
nodes.rationale: Grid gap, card padding, component chrome first; putting the badge and title on one row gave back ~74px on every slide.

nodes.label: Fill width with type size, not a stretched column
nodes.rationale: A minmax(0,1fr) description column only moves the emptiness to one side; 58% fill at 34px became 94% at 37/38px.
nodes.norm_label: fill width with type size, not a stretched column

nodes.label: Footer number is machine-written
nodes.rationale: Written to .deck-foot > .deck-foot__num (direct child only). Never hand-maintain page numbers; keep the day label nested inside .deck-foot__side or it gets clobbered.

nodes.label: .sag-slide__head is a grid with hard-coded placement
nodes.rationale: Badge row 1 col 1, title row 1 col 2, rule and lead row 2; a third element dropped directly in the head lands in an unplaced auto row.
nodes.norm_label: .sag-slide__head is a grid with hard-coded placement

nodes.label: A tooltip host must be position: relative
nodes.rationale: Otherwise bottom: calc(100% + 10px) resolves against the slide and the tip lands 1090px up, in the DOM but invisible.
nodes.norm_label: a tooltip host must be position: relative

nodes.label: .snipbox__copy must be a sibling of the <pre>
nodes.rationale: As a child, its icon glyph is copied along with the command. It floats on hover so it reserves no space.
nodes.norm_label: .snipbox__copy must be a sibling of the <pre>

nodes.label: .snip and .kbd have hard-coded light backgrounds
nodes.rationale: Do not put them on a dark slide.

nodes.label: .qmark must be <button type=button>
nodes.rationale: Inside a task row it relies on stopPropagation to avoid ticking the row.

nodes.label: A duplicated data-task-key couples unrelated rows
nodes.rationale: Silent; two different tasks start ticking together.
nodes.norm_label: a duplicated data-task-key couples unrelated rows

nodes.label: Grep class values for non-ASCII after hand edits
nodes.rationale: deck-foot__num once became deك-foot__num and would have silently lost its styling.
nodes.norm_label: grep class values for non-ascii after hand edits

nodes.label: Test over file://, not http://localhost
nodes.rationale: Python's http.server has no Range support, so video seeking appears broken when it is fine. The real presentation is always file://.

nodes.label: navigator.clipboard rejects under file://
nodes.rationale: Silently; the execCommand fallback is mandatory. Do not 'modernise' it away.

nodes.label: Scope verification queries to the active slide
nodes.rationale: A global selector once returned a tooltip from a different slide entirely.
nodes.norm_label: scope verification queries to the active slide

nodes.label: A CSS comment can swallow the rules after it
nodes.rationale: Prose accidentally placed after */ silently killed three rules; the symptom was a value reverting with no diff to explain it.
nodes.norm_label: a css comment can swallow the rules after it

nodes.label: day-deck-recipe.md
nodes.rationale: How to build day-NN.html for days 2-10 without re-deciding anything Day 1 already settled.

nodes.label: Day 1 is not the template
nodes.rationale: Day 1 carries ~18 slides of one-time onboarding (package tour, legend, Claude Code basics, skills map, 29-task map) that never recur; days 2-10 are much smaller and share one skeleton.

nodes.label: Day deck skeleton (days 2-10)
nodes.rationale: Cover; two day-plan slides; goals; theory slides per section each followed by that section's recording slide; break «عملك على مشروعك»; «دورك الآن» checklist; break «مراجعة وعرض التقدم»; review; tomorrow.

nodes.label: Goals slide comes LAST in the plan block
nodes.rationale: «أهداف اليوم» follows the tasks, never precedes them (CLAUDE.md A.6.8).
nodes.norm_label: goals slide comes last in the plan block

nodes.label: Slides 2-3: day plan with .sess columns
nodes.rationale: Slide 2: شرح المفاهيم + تطبيق مع المدرب; slide 3: عملك على مشروعك + مراجعة; each a 2 x .sess block copied verbatim from the curriculum's ### 2.N rows.

nodes.label: ▶ المقطع: §A (stepvid recording slide)
nodes.rationale: Per section: the stepvid slide of that section's tasks performed for real; the trainer then re-runs it live with no slide.

nodes.label: «دورك الآن» nested task checklist (light)
nodes.rationale: Nested checklist on a LIGHT surface, preceded by the عملك break; always the highest overflow risk in a day.

nodes.label: Review and tomorrow slides
nodes.rationale: «مراجعة اليوم» then «غدًا — اليوم N+1».

nodes.label: Two break slides from Day 2, never three
nodes.rationale: Explain and live are delivered interleaved, so there is no transition to mark between them, and the day opens on شرح المفاهيم so a 'we start now' slide there marks nothing. Day 1 is the exception and keeps three.
nodes.norm_label: two break slides from day 2, never three

nodes.label: Both sessions run every day, together
nodes.rationale: Per section: (1) trainer explains the concepts, (2) the recording plays, (3) the trainer executes the same steps live. They are not alternatives and not two blocks. Day 1 is the only whole-day exception (its first session is course preparation that can't be re-executed live).
nodes.norm_label: both sessions run every day, together

nodes.label: Watched-not-re-run exception
nodes.rationale: A one-time, account-bound section is watched, not re-run live (step 3 drops; steps 1-2 stay). Test: would a second live performance produce anything? Deploying an already-deployed project does not. Known cases listed: §16 first deploy (Day 3) and §16.3 final redeploy (Day 10), decided 2026-09-25.

nodes.label: Exception is re-earned per section
nodes.rationale: §12 (Day 5) sits next to §7.11.3 (Day 4), which the text says does get the exception, but §12's task is neither one-time nor account-bound, so it doesn't. Check the test for the section in front of you instead of assuming it propagates. Note the 'Known cases' line omits §7.11.3 although this passage says it gets the exception.

nodes.label: Watched sections: say it on the slide
nodes.rationale: The recording slide's title or badge must state it is watched and the day-plan session note must match; silently dropping the live third looks like an omission. Do not touch the minute budget: time goes to watching, explaining and answering.
nodes.norm_label: watched sections: say it on the slide

nodes.label: Ship the slide anyway when the recording is missing
nodes.rationale: A day's recordings are usually filmed after its deck is built, and the steps are knowable from the curriculum's own numbered steps. Waiting is the wrong default and so is faking timestamps; use stepvid__video--soon.
nodes.norm_label: ship the slide anyway when the recording is missing

nodes.label: stepvid__video--soon placeholder markup
nodes.rationale:
Dashed box with

المقطع تحت التصوير

; steps use ordinals (the example shows an Arabic-Indic ١).

nodes.label: No <video>, no data-t, no time button while pending
nodes.rationale: A dead 0:00 that seeks nowhere is a worse lie than an honest dashed box; initStepVideos skips a step with no data-t so the placeholder costs nothing at runtime. Write steps as the trainee will experience them (not a shot list) and log the planned filename and scope in MEDIA_SHOTLIST marked ⬜.
nodes.norm_label: no <video>, no data-t, no time button while pending

nodes.label: After filming: swap box, convert ordinals, re-check frames
nodes.rationale: Swap for a real <video>, turn every ordinal into its data-t, and re-check each step against extracted frames, not the transcript. Auto-generated summaries have been wrong about the editor, the paste target and an entire edited-out exchange.
nodes.norm_label: after filming: swap box, convert ordinals, re-check frames

nodes.label: Icon set is closed (22 icons)
nodes.rationale: No video, film, camera or play icon exists; i-clock is the one for a تحت التصوير box. An undefined class i i-… renders nothing at all (a CSS mask with no source) and deckAudit will not catch it. Grep icons.css before using a new icon name.

nodes.label: Every day totals 215 minutes plus 25 break
nodes.rationale: Stated at bootcamp_roadmap_and_curriculum.md:68 as fixed for every day. The four session durations on slides 2-3 must add up; never inflate a total, reallocate inside a band. Day 2: شرح 48 + تطبيق 58 + عملك 82 + مراجعة 27 = 215.
nodes.norm_label: every day totals 215 minutes plus 25 break

nodes.label: Build order (seven steps)
nodes.rationale: 1 read the curriculum ### 2.N block first; 2 read the day's ## N sections; 3 grep «صياغة مقترحة» and account for every hit; 4 read the matching skills; 5 check where output lands in PRODUCT.md; 6 copy the skeleton and fill from day-01.html; 7 verify then sync the day's brief and MEDIA_SHOTLIST.

nodes.label: Step 1: copy task rows verbatim from curriculum
nodes.rationale: Section number, duration and parenthetical note become slides 2-3 and the «دورك الآن» checklist. The deck never invents a task.
nodes.norm_label: step 1: copy task rows verbatim from curriculum

nodes.label: Step 3: every «صياغة مقترحة» must reach a slide
nodes.rationale: Ready-made prompts are half of the deliberate redundancy CLAUDE.md A.5 requires, and the slide is the half the trainee reads. Count before building and after. Incident: §9's two prompts were missed while §8's neighbouring pair were on slides, so nothing looked wrong.
nodes.norm_label: step 3: every «صياغة مقترحة» must reach a slide

nodes.label: Step 4: read the matching skill first
nodes.rationale: The slides must not teach something the skill will contradict when Claude executes it live.
nodes.norm_label: step 4: read the matching skill first

nodes.label: Step 5: check where the output lands in PRODUCT.md
nodes.rationale: If the slide promises a three-column table and PRODUCT.md has two, one of them is wrong; fix before shipping.
nodes.norm_label: step 5: check where the output lands in product.md

nodes.label: Sub-durations render as separate task rows
nodes.rationale: A curriculum line like `12.1 15 د · 12.2 10 د · 12.3 12 د · 12.4 46 د` reads better as four .task rows on both the agenda slide and the checklist than force-fit into one task__t/task__d pair: same total, not crammed.
nodes.norm_label: sub-durations render as separate task rows

nodes.label: Task keys: same tasks in two places
nodes.rationale: The day-plan rows and «دورك الآن» are the same tasks; give each an explicit data-task-key so ticking either moves both and hang subtasks off the parent with data-parent. localStorage is namespaced by filename (sag-deck:day-02.html:tasks), so key names can be reused day to day.
nodes.norm_label: task keys: same tasks in two places

nodes.label: What does not carry across days
nodes.rationale: data-ref cannot cross files, checkbox state is per file, and the ؟ window reads one template per slide, so a Day-1 term must be re-explained when Day 2 needs it.
nodes.norm_label: what does not carry across days

nodes.label: Restate in a short recap slide, not a pointer
nodes.rationale: Day 2's الغاية/الخاصية recap exists for exactly this reason.
nodes.norm_label: restate in a short recap slide, not a pointer

nodes.label: Verification (same gate as Day 1)
nodes.rationale: deckAudit (nested checklist is highest risk), deckRefAudit = [], checkbox behaviour in a browser, register sweeps on the new file, every «صياغة مقترحة» on a slide, durations sum to 215, commands as .snipbox, offline, screenshot and read the cover, goals slide, each showcase slide and the checklist.

nodes.label: Register sweeps on the new file
nodes.rationale: و+Latin glue = 0; «طرفية» = 0; the سوي verb family (يسو/تسو/نسو/سوّ) = 0; no row or title opening with a و-word; singular address. Sweep the family, never one spelling: the first real family sweep (2026-09-25) found three live «تسوّي» on Day 1. Known false positive: noun «المسوّدة».
nodes.norm_label: register sweeps on the new file

nodes.label: Offline: no remote font/stylesheet/script/image
nodes.rationale: Same offline rule as the main skill checklist.

nodes.label: ميثاق العمل — كيف أتصرّف دائمًا
nodes.rationale: Loaded in full on every message so it stays short; audience is Claude only, the trainee never reads it. Says HOW to behave always; WHO/WHERE lives in CLAUDE.md, per-section execution in skills.

nodes.label: عقد الملفات — كل ملف يجيب عن سؤال واحد
nodes.rationale: Prevents content duplication between files: never write in one file what belongs to another.
nodes.norm_label: عقد الملفات — كل ملف يجيب عن سوال واحد

nodes.label: التكرار المقصود — صيغ المطالبات في موضعين
nodes.rationale: Prompt templates live in both the skill and the trainee-facing material so work continues even if Claude fails and the trainee can be explicit; never 'clean it up'.
nodes.norm_label: التكرار المقصود — صيغ المطالبات في موضعين

nodes.label: conversation_history.md — ذاكرة المشروع الدائمة
nodes.rationale: Survives context-window limits, session restarts and model switches; a new session reads it to restore context.

nodes.label: الدورة الإلزامية في كل رسالة: أنشئ ← مطالبة ← ردّ كامل ← أسطر دردشة
nodes.rationale: File first, chat second: whoever writes chat first ends up abbreviating the file, which corrupts the log.
nodes.norm_label: الدورة الالزامية في كل رسالة: انشي ← مطالبة ← رد كامل ← اسطر دردشة

nodes.label: اختبار المخالفة: ما في الملف أطول من الدردشة دائمًا
nodes.rationale: Chat is the pointer, the file is the copy; if chat is longer the rule was violated. If the trainee has to ask to document it, Claude forgot.
nodes.norm_label: اختبار المخالفة: ما في الملف اطول من الدردشة دايما

nodes.label: استثناء الأسرار الإلزامي — اكتب <تم استلام المفتاح>
nodes.rationale: 'Document everything' does not include keys or passwords.
nodes.norm_label: استثناء الاسرار الالزامي — اكتب <تم استلام المفتاح>
